source: Written 2026-10-23/24 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2017 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC17.6.RP.1: Unit rates are left to NC.6.RP.2 and percents to NC.6.RP.3; this part covers ratio meaning, language, tables, tape diagrams, double number lines and graph points.
notes.NC17.6.RP.3: 30 questions written. Skills: ratio tables and equivalent ratios 6, unit ratio and unit rate 5, measurement conversions 6, graphs of value pairs (written as ordered pairs) 6, comparing ratios and rates 3, part-to-part and part-to-whole 4. Percent is left out (not in the summary). Graphs are given only as lists of points.
notes.NC17.6.NS.1: Visual models (strips, number lines) cannot be shown, so meaning is asked in words: how many halves fit in 4, which question a division answers, which multiplication matches. Skills (rough counts): whole number divided by a fraction 5, fraction divided by a whole number 5, fraction divided by a fraction 6, mixed numbers 3, interpreting a quotient 5, word problems 6 (more word-problem contexts also sit under the first three skills). Fractions in answers are given as a/b or mixed numbers.
notes.NC17.6.NS.3: Answers are terminating decimals throughout (grade 6 standard algorithms). Division quotients always end; 27 divided by 8 is the only whole-number-to-decimal case.
notes.NC17.6.NS.4: GCF of numbers to 100 and LCM of numbers to 12 are asked as the standard states; fractions appear through simplest form and the least common denominator.
notes.NC17.6.NS.5: Skills (rough counts): positive and negative numbers for opposite quantities (6), meaning of zero in context (4), absolute value as distance from zero (5), absolute value as magnitude in context (4), rational numbers as signed quantities (4), opposite of a number (2), comparing magnitudes (3), numbers with a given absolute value (2). No question orders signed numbers by value or finds distances between points (6.NS.7 and 6.NS.8). Money is written in words with no dollar sign.
notes.NC17.6.NS.6: Thirty questions on rational numbers on a number line and in the coordinate plane. The number line and the plane are described in words and coordinates; reflections are across the axes only. No distances between points (a later standard).
notes.NC17.6.EE.1: Bases and exponents are whole numbers only (no negative or fractional bases, no zero exponent), as the standard says.
notes.NC17.6.EE.4: Whole-number coefficients, one half in one question; no negative answers. Property names in the justification questions are the grade 6 ones (commutative, associative, identity, distributive).
notes.NC17.6.EE.5: Equations only (the summary names equations), so no inequalities. Exponent equations use whole-number values only; no negative numbers. Contexts give the equation and ask which value from a set makes it true.
notes.NC17.6.EE.6: Writing an expression has a choice answer, so 21 of 30 are choice questions. The 9 numeric questions have the student form the expression from the story and then use it for a given value of the variable; no equation-solving (6.EE.7) and no named parts of an expression (6.EE.2b).
notes.NC17.6.EE.7: One-step equations x + p = q and px = q with whole numbers, decimals and fractions (nonnegative answers). Solving by hand; writing an equation from a story or matching a story to an equation is asked as choice questions (the equation options are the only choices that carry a variable name; the others use letters as in the question).
notes.NC17.6.EE.8: Only > and < are used, as the summary says (x > c or x < c); no at least / at most / greater-or-equal wording. Number line graphs are described in words (open or closed circle, direction of shading).
notes.NC17.6.G.2: Fractional-edge volume only: whole-number answers where friendly, otherwise fractions or mixed numbers. Choice answers carry their unit so all four options end alike. No cube roots or unit conversions (outside grade 6).
notes.NC17.6.G.3: Drawing the polygon is asked through its vertices in words; no picture is shown. Side lengths only on sides sharing a coordinate (horizontal or vertical), with coordinates in all four quadrants (Grade 6).
notes.NC17.6.G.4: Nets are described in words (the faces they contain), never drawn. Answers are whole numbers or short decimals; slant heights are given, never derived.
notes.NC17.6.SP.1: Recognising a statistical question is mostly a choice task, so only 6 of 30 are numeric (counts of how many questions in a list are statistical or not, and how many different answers there are); a bare number cannot test the idea fairly otherwise. Only everyday contexts with a clear single answer or clear variability are used; borderline questions were avoided.
notes.NC17.6.SP.2: Distributions of data are written as lists of values/counts since no dot plots or histograms can be shown. Spread is tested with the range only (no IQR or MAD, which belong to SP.5).
notes.NC17.6.SP.3: Quartiles are defined in the stem as the median of each half, so no convention is assumed; MAD is defined in the stem.
notes.NC17.6.SP.4: Dot plots, histograms and box plots are written out as counts at each value, bar heights per interval, and five-number summaries; no pictures. Quartiles use the median of each half.
notes.NC17.6.SP.5: Thirty questions: observations and units, mean, median, range, IQR, MAD, shape (symmetry, skew, clusters, gaps, outliers) and choosing a measure. Data are written as lists; a dot plot, histogram or box plot is not shown, so shape is read from a list of values. Standard deviation is not used (not a Grade 6 skill).

questions.skill: Writing a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: A bag has 3 red marbles and 5 blue marbles. Which is the ratio of red marbles to blue marbles?
questions.solution: Red comes first, so the ratio is red to blue: 3 to 5. The ratio 5 to 3 has the order reversed, and 8 is the total number of marbles.

solve.work: 3 red to 5 blue, in that order: 3 to 5.

questions.stem: A bowl has 4 apples and 6 oranges. The ratio of apples to all the fruit is 4 to ?. What is the ?
questions.solution: All the fruit is $4 + 6 = 10$ pieces, so the ratio of apples to all the fruit is 4 to 10.

solve.work: All fruit = 4+6 = 10, so apples to all fruit is 4 to 10.

questions.stem: The ratio of cats to dogs at a shelter is 2 to 7. Which sentence is true?
choices: For every 7 cats there are 2 dogs
For every 2 cats there are 5 dogs
For every 9 cats there are 2 dogs
For every 2 cats there are 7 dogs
questions.answer: For every 2 cats there are 7 dogs
questions.solution: A ratio of cats to dogs of 2 to 7 means 2 cats for every 7 dogs. The other sentences swap the order or use the total of 9 animals.

solve.answer: For every 2 cats there are 7 dogs
solve.work: 2 to 7 cats to dogs means for every 2 cats there are 7 dogs.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour for every 1 cup of sugar. How many cups of flour go with 5 cups of sugar?
questions.solution: Each cup of sugar goes with 2 cups of flour, so 5 cups of sugar go with $2 \times 5 = 10$ cups of flour.

solve.work: 2 cups flour per 1 cup sugar; 5 cups sugar -> 2*5 = 10 cups flour.

questions.skill: Writing a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: Maya has 6 hats and 9 scarves. Which ratio compares her scarves to her hats?
questions.solution: Scarves are named first, so the ratio is scarves to hats: 9 to 6. The ratio 6 to 9 has the order reversed, and 15 is the total number of items.

solve.work: Scarves to hats, in that order: 9 to 6.

questions.stem: In a ratio table, 1 bike has 2 wheels, 2 bikes have 4 wheels and 3 bikes have 6 wheels. How many wheels do 7 bikes have?
questions.solution: Each bike adds 2 wheels, so 7 bikes have $7 \times 2 = 14$ wheels.

questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to 1 to 4?
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 2: $1 \times 2 = 2$ and $4 \times 2 = 8$, giving 2 to 8. Adding 1 to both numbers, swapping them, or changing only one of them does not keep the ratio.

solve.work: Multiply both by 2: 1 to 4 = 2 to 8. 1 to 8, 4 to 1, 2 to 5 are not equivalent.

questions.stem: A tape diagram for a bead ratio has 3 equal parts for blue beads and 2 equal parts for green beads. Each part stands for 4 beads. How many blue beads are there?
questions.solution: The blue beads fill 3 parts of 4 beads each: $3 \times 4 = 12$ blue beads.

questions.stem: A club has 7 boys and 9 girls. Which ratio compares the boys to all the students in the club?
questions.solution: All the students are $7 + 9 = 16$. Boys to all the students is 7 to 16.

solve.work: All students = 7+9 = 16; boys to all = 7 to 16.

questions.stem: The ratio of ducks to geese on a pond is 5 to 2. There are 10 ducks. How many geese are there?
questions.solution: 10 ducks is 2 groups of 5 ducks. Each group has 2 geese, so there are $2 \times 2 = 4$ geese.

solve.work: 5 ducks : 2 geese; 10 ducks is 5*2, so geese = 2*2 = 4.

questions.stem: Which row of a ratio table matches "for every 2 apples there are 3 oranges"?
questions.solution: Doubling both numbers of 2 apples and 3 oranges gives 4 apples and 6 oranges. The ratio stays 2 to 3.

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: A pen holds 2 hens for every 1 rooster. How many hens are in the pen if it has 6 roosters?
questions.solution: Each rooster goes with 2 hens. 6 roosters go with 6 x 2 = 12 hens.

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: For every 3 red tiles in a mosaic there are 4 blue tiles. The mosaic has 12 red tiles. How many blue tiles does it have?
questions.solution: 12 red tiles is 4 groups of 3 red tiles. Each group goes with 4 blue tiles, so there are 4 x 4 = 16 blue tiles.

questions.stem: A double number line has cups of flour on the top and cups of sugar on the bottom. The mark 2 on the top lines up with 4 on the bottom, and 3 on the top lines up with 6 on the bottom. Which is the ratio of cups of flour to cups of sugar?
questions.solution: Each cup of flour lines up with 2 cups of sugar, so the ratio of flour to sugar is 1 to 2. The ratio 2 to 1 puts the quantities in the wrong order.

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: A class has 12 girls and 15 boys. The ratio of girls to all the students is 12 to ?. What is the ?
questions.solution: All the students are 12 girls + 15 boys = 27 students, so the ratio of girls to all the students is 12 to 27.

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: In a choir, 6 of the 10 singers are altos. Which is the ratio of altos to all the singers?
questions.solution: The altos are 6 and all the singers are 10, so the ratio of altos to all the singers is 6 to 10.

questions.stem: Which is another way to write the ratio 5 to 9?
questions.solution: The ratio 5 to 9 can be written 5:9, with the numbers in the same order. 9:5 is reversed.

questions.stem: A box has 10 red crayons and 15 blue crayons. The ratio 10 to 15 written in simplest form is 2 to ?. What is the ?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 5: 10 / 5 = 2 and 15 / 5 = 3. The ratio is 2 to 3.

questions.stem: A ratio table has the pairs 1 and 5, 2 and 10, 3 and 15. Which rule connects the first number to the second number?
questions.solution: 1 x 5 = 5, 2 x 5 = 10 and 3 x 5 = 15, so each second number is the first number times 5.

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: Mia has 4 pencils and 9 pens. Which ratio compares her pencils to all the pens and pencils she has?
questions.solution: All the pens and pencils are 4 + 9 = 13. The ratio of pencils to all of them is 4 to 13.

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: A fruit bowl holds 8 pears and 3 bananas. Which is the ratio of bananas to pears?
questions.solution: The ratio of bananas to pears puts the bananas first: 3 bananas to 8 pears, or 3 to 8.

questions.stem: At a park the ratio of dogs to cats is 1 to 3. Which sentence is true?
choices: There are 3 cats for every dog
There are 3 dogs for every cat
There are 3 more cats than dogs
There are 4 pets for every cat
questions.answer: There are 3 cats for every dog
questions.solution: In the ratio 1 to 3 the first number is dogs and the second is cats, so there are 3 cats for every 1 dog.

solve.answer: There are 3 cats for every dog
solve.work: 1 dog to 3 cats means 3 cats for every dog. Others misread the ratio or treat it as a difference.

questions.stem: A ratio table for trail mix shows 2 cups of nuts with 3 cups of raisins, and 4 cups of nuts with 6 cups of raisins. How many cups of raisins go with 8 cups of nuts?
questions.solution: Every time the nuts go up by 2 cups, the raisins go up by 3 cups. 8 cups of nuts is 4 groups of 2, so there are 4 x 3 = 12 cups of raisins.

questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to 3 to 5?
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 3: 3 x 3 = 9 and 5 x 3 = 15. The other options add the same number to both, which does not keep the ratio.

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: A recipe uses 1 cup of rice for every 2 cups of water. How many cups of water go with 6 cups of rice?
questions.solution: Each cup of rice goes with 2 cups of water. 6 cups of rice go with 6 x 2 = 12 cups of water.

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: A zoo has 3 lions for every 2 tigers. The zoo has 10 tigers. How many lions does it have?
questions.solution: 10 tigers is 5 groups of 2 tigers. Each group goes with 3 lions, so there are 5 x 3 = 15 lions.

questions.stem: A tape diagram has 2 equal boxes for Jo's marbles and 5 equal boxes of the same size for Sam's marbles. Which is the ratio of Jo's marbles to Sam's marbles?
questions.solution: Jo has 2 boxes and Sam has 5 boxes of the same size, so the ratio of Jo's marbles to Sam's marbles is 2 to 5.

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: A team has 7 players and 5 of them are girls. The ratio of girls to boys on the team is 5 to ?. What is the ?
questions.solution: The boys are 7 - 5 = 2 players. The ratio of girls to boys is 5 to 2.

questions.stem: A tape diagram for stickers has 4 equal parts for star stickers and 1 equal part for heart stickers. Each part stands for 3 stickers. How many star stickers are there?
questions.solution: There are 4 equal parts of star stickers, and each part is 3 stickers: 4 x 3 = 12 star stickers.

questions.stem: Which does NOT show the ratio of 3 squares to 7 circles?
questions.solution: The ratio of squares to circles starts with the 3 squares, so it is 3 to 7, 3:7 or 3 for every 7. The ratio 7:3 puts the circles first.

solve.work: 3 squares to 7 circles is 3:7; 7:3 reverses it.

questions.skill: Ratios as points on a graph
questions.stem: Each point (x, y) shows x notebooks and y pencils in a gift pack. The points (1, 4), (2, 8) and (3, 12) lie on one line through (0, 0). How many pencils go with 5 notebooks?
questions.solution: Each notebook goes with 4 pencils, so 5 notebooks go with 5 x 4 = 20 pencils.

solve.work: Points lie on y=4x (4 pencils per notebook). x=5 gives y=20.

questions.stem: On a double number line, miles are on the top and minutes are on the bottom. The mark 1 mile lines up with 10 minutes, and 2 miles lines up with 20 minutes. How many minutes line up with 5 miles?
questions.solution: Each mile lines up with 10 minutes, so 5 miles line up with 5 x 10 = 50 minutes.

questions.stem: In a bag, the ratio of red marbles to blue marbles is 3:5. Which sentence says the same thing?
choices: For every 3 red marbles there are 5 blue marbles
For every 5 red marbles there are 3 blue marbles
Red marbles make up 3 out of every 5 marbles
For every 3 red marbles there are 8 blue marbles
questions.answer: For every 3 red marbles there are 5 blue marbles
questions.solution: In 3:5 the first number is red and the second is blue, so there are 5 blue marbles for every 3 red ones. Red marbles are 3 out of every 8, not 3 out of every 5.

solve.answer: For every 3 red marbles there are 5 blue marbles
solve.work: 3:5 red to blue = for every 3 red, 5 blue.

questions.skill: Writing a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: A team won 9 games and lost 6 games. The ratio of wins to losses in simplest form is 3 to ?. What is the ?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers of 9 to 6 by 3: $9 \div 3 = 3$ and $6 \div 3 = 2$. The ratio is 3 to 2.

questions.stem: Which pair of ratios is equivalent?
questions.solution: Both 6 to 10 and 9 to 15 simplify to 3 to 5. Adding 3 to each number (9 to 13), swapping the order (10 to 6), or changing the numbers by different factors (12 to 15) does not give an equivalent ratio.

questions.stem: A ratio table shows cups of juice and cups of water in a punch: 2 and 5, then 4 and 10, then 6 and 15. How many cups of water go with 10 cups of juice?
questions.solution: Each 2 cups of juice go with 5 cups of water. 10 cups of juice is 5 groups of 2, so the water is $5 \times 5 = 25$ cups.

questions.stem: The ratio of nickels to dimes in a jar is 3 to 4. Which statement must be true?
choices: If there are 9 nickels, there are 10 dimes
If there are 9 nickels, there are 3 dimes
If there are 9 nickels, there are 36 dimes
If there are 9 nickels, there are 12 dimes
questions.answer: If there are 9 nickels, there are 12 dimes
questions.solution: Going from 3 nickels to 9 nickels multiplies by 3, so the 4 dimes are multiplied by 3 too: 12 dimes. Adding the same amount to both, dividing by 3, or multiplying by 4 breaks the ratio.

solve.answer: If there are 9 nickels, there are 12 dimes

questions.stem: A tape diagram for a mix has 2 equal parts for sand and 5 equal parts for gravel. The sand is 6 buckets. How many buckets of gravel are there?
questions.solution: Two parts of sand are 6 buckets, so 1 part is $6 \div 2 = 3$ buckets. The 5 parts of gravel are $5 \times 3 = 15$ buckets.

questions.stem: Which tape diagram matches the ratio 3 to 2 of apples to pears?
choices: 2 equal boxes for apples and 3 equal boxes of the same size for pears
3 equal boxes for apples and 2 equal boxes of the same size for pears
3 equal boxes for apples and 5 equal boxes of the same size for pears
5 equal boxes for apples and 2 equal boxes of the same size for pears
questions.answer: 3 equal boxes for apples and 2 equal boxes of the same size for pears
questions.solution: The ratio 3 to 2 is shown by 3 boxes for apples and 2 boxes for pears, all the same size. Swapping the counts, or using the total of 5, shows a different ratio.

solve.answer: 3 equal boxes for apples and 2 equal boxes of the same size for pears
solve.work: Apples 3 boxes, pears 2 boxes of same size.

questions.stem: At a school there are 24 students for every 2 teachers. At that ratio, how many students go with 5 teachers?
questions.solution: Each teacher goes with $24 \div 2 = 12$ students, so 5 teachers go with $5 \times 12 = 60$ students.

questions.skill: Writing a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: Ken has 8 red pens and 12 black pens. Which statement about the ratio of black pens to red pens is true?
choices: It is 8 to 12, which is equivalent to 3 to 2
It is 12 to 8, which is equivalent to 4 to 3
It is 12 to 20, which is equivalent to 3 to 5
It is 12 to 8, which is equivalent to 3 to 2
questions.answer: It is 12 to 8, which is equivalent to 3 to 2
questions.solution: Black comes first, so the ratio is 12 to 8. Dividing both numbers by 4 gives 3 to 2. The other options reverse the order, simplify wrongly, or use the total of 20 pens.

solve.answer: It is 12 to 8, which is equivalent to 3 to 2
solve.work: Black to red = 12 to 8 = 3 to 2 (divide by 4). 4 to 3 is wrong; 8 to 12 is the wrong order.

questions.stem: In a ratio table of blue paint to white paint, the blue column reads 3, 6, ?, 12 and the white column reads 2, 4, 6, 8. What number replaces the ?
questions.solution: The row with 6 cans of white is 3 times the first row (2 cans of white), so the blue is $3 \times 3 = 9$ cans.

questions.stem: Which ratio is NOT equivalent to 12 to 18?
questions.solution: 12 to 18 simplifies to 2 to 3. The ratios 6 to 9 and 8 to 12 also simplify to 2 to 3, but 4 to 7 does not.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 2 cups of oats with 3 cups of milk. A bigger batch uses 6 cups of oats. Zoe says it needs 7 cups of milk, because 6 is 4 more than 2. Which statement is correct?
choices: It needs 7 cups of milk, because both amounts go up by the same number
It needs 8 cups of milk, because the amount of milk doubles
It needs 12 cups of milk, because the amount of milk is multiplied by 4
It needs 9 cups of milk, because both amounts are multiplied by 3
questions.answer: It needs 9 cups of milk, because both amounts are multiplied by 3
questions.solution: To keep the ratio, multiply both amounts by the same number. 2 x 3 = 6, so 3 x 3 = 9 cups of milk. Adding 4 to both amounts does not keep the ratio.

solve.answer: It needs 9 cups of milk, because both amounts are multiplied by 3
solve.work: 6/2 = 3, so milk is 3×3 = 9 cups (multiplicative, not additive).

questions.stem: A tape diagram for a class has 3 equal parts for girls and 4 equal parts for boys of the same size. There are 28 students in all. How many girls are there?
questions.solution: There are 3 + 4 = 7 equal parts in all. 28 / 7 = 4 students in each part. The girls are 3 parts, so 3 x 4 = 12 girls.

questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to 20 to 36?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 4: 20 / 4 = 5 and 36 / 4 = 9. The ratio 10 to 26 comes from subtracting 10, which does not keep the ratio.

questions.stem: Mei and Lou share 45 stickers in the ratio 4 to 5. A tape diagram shows 4 equal parts for Mei and 5 equal parts for Lou. How many stickers does Lou get?
questions.solution: There are 4 + 5 = 9 equal parts. 45 / 9 = 5 stickers in each part. Lou has 5 parts, so 5 x 5 = 25 stickers.

questions.stem: A ratio table shows pages read and minutes: 6 pages in 9 minutes, ? pages in 15 minutes, and 18 pages in 27 minutes. What number replaces the ?
questions.solution: 6 pages in 9 minutes is 2 pages for every 3 minutes (divide both by 3). 15 minutes is 5 groups of 3 minutes, so 5 x 2 = 10 pages.

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: A store has 12 laptops and 8 tablets. Which statement is true?
choices: There are 3 tablets for every 2 laptops
There are 3 laptops for every 5 tablets
There are 5 laptops for every 3 tablets
There are 3 laptops for every 2 tablets
questions.answer: There are 3 laptops for every 2 tablets
questions.solution: The ratio of laptops to tablets is 12 to 8. Divide both by 4 to get 3 to 2: 3 laptops for every 2 tablets.

solve.answer: There are 3 laptops for every 2 tablets

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: Of 30 trees in a park, 24 are maples. Which statement is true?
choices: The ratio of maples to all trees is 4 to 1
The ratio of maples to other trees is 4 to 1
The ratio of other trees to maples is 4 to 1
The ratio of other trees to all trees is 4 to 1
questions.answer: The ratio of maples to other trees is 4 to 1
questions.solution: There are 30 - 24 = 6 other trees. Maples to other trees is 24 to 6, or 4 to 1. Maples to all trees is 24 to 30, or 4 to 5.

solve.answer: The ratio of maples to other trees is 4 to 1

questions.stem: A double number line shows minutes on the top and pages read on the bottom, at a steady pace. The mark 4 minutes lines up with 6 pages. Which mark on the top lines up with 18 pages?
questions.solution: 18 pages is 3 times 6 pages, so the minutes are 3 times 4 minutes, which is 12 minutes. Adding 12 to both numbers would give 16 minutes, which is not the same pace.

questions.stem: The ratio of salt to water in a brine is 1 to 20. Which mixture has the same ratio?
choices: 2 tablespoons of salt and 22 cups of water
1 tablespoon of salt and 21 cups of water
2 tablespoons of salt and 40 cups of water
20 tablespoons of salt and 1 cup of water
questions.answer: 2 tablespoons of salt and 40 cups of water
questions.solution: Multiplying both numbers of 1 to 20 by 2 gives 2 to 40. Adding the same amount to both would not keep the ratio.

solve.answer: 2 tablespoons of salt and 40 cups of water

questions.stem: A tape diagram shows 2 equal parts for Lena's money and 7 equal parts of the same size for Omar's money. Omar has 35 dollars. Which equation finds the value $p$ of one part?
questions.solution: Omar's money is 7 equal parts and he has 35 dollars, so 7p = 35. Then p = 5 dollars.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: Water and juice are mixed in the ratio 3 to 5. How many cups of juice are in 40 cups of the mix?
questions.solution: There are 3 + 5 = 8 parts in the mix. 40 / 8 = 5 cups in each part. The juice is 5 parts, so 5 x 5 = 25 cups.

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: A lemonade uses 3 cups of lemon juice for every 8 cups of water. How many cups of lemon juice go with 32 cups of water?
questions.solution: 32 cups of water is 4 groups of 8 cups. Each group goes with 3 cups of lemon juice, so 4 x 3 = 12 cups.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of fiction books to nonfiction books on a shelf is 5 to 3. There are 15 fiction books. How many books are on the shelf in all?
questions.solution: 15 fiction books is 3 groups of 5. So there are 3 groups of 3 nonfiction books, which is 9. In all, 15 + 9 = 24 books.

questions.stem: Pia has 2 red beads for every 3 blue beads on a bracelet. The bracelet has 15 beads in all. Which is true?
questions.solution: Each group of 2 red and 3 blue has 5 beads. 15 / 5 = 3 groups, so there are 3 x 2 = 6 red beads and 3 x 3 = 9 blue beads.

solve.work: Ratio 2:3, 5 beads per group; 15/5 = 3 groups; red 2x3 = 6, blue 3x3 = 9.

questions.stem: Which statement about ratios is true?
choices: Multiplying both numbers of a ratio by 4 gives an equivalent ratio
Adding 4 to both numbers of a ratio gives an equivalent ratio
Reversing the order of the two numbers gives an equivalent ratio
Subtracting 4 from both numbers of a ratio gives an equivalent ratio
questions.answer: Multiplying both numbers of a ratio by 4 gives an equivalent ratio
questions.solution: An equivalent ratio comes from multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number. Adding or subtracting does not keep the ratio, and reversing the order changes what is compared.

solve.answer: Multiplying both numbers of a ratio by 4 gives an equivalent ratio
solve.work: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying (or dividing) both numbers by the same nonzero number. Adding/subtracting or reversing does not (e.g. 1:2 vs 5:6, 2:1).

questions.stem: On a double number line, hours are on the top and dollars earned are on the bottom, at a steady rate. The mark 2 hours lines up with 14 dollars. How many dollars line up with 5 hours?
questions.solution: 2 hours line up with 14 dollars, so 1 hour lines up with 7 dollars. 5 hours line up with 5 x 7 = 35 dollars.

questions.skill: Ratios as points on a graph
questions.stem: Each point (x, y) shows x cups of flour and y cups of sugar. The points (4, 6) and (6, 9) lie on a line through (0, 0). A point on this line has x equal to 10. What is its y?
questions.solution: The ratio of x to y is 4 to 6, which is 2 to 3. 10 is 5 groups of 2, so y is 5 x 3 = 15.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of Sam's cats to his dogs is 3 to 2. He has 6 cats. How many pets does he have in all?
questions.solution: 6 cats is 2 groups of 3 cats. So he has 2 groups of 2 dogs, which is 4 dogs. In all, 6 + 4 = 10 pets.

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of the length to the width of a poster is 7 to 4. The width is 20 centimeters. What is the length in centimeters?
questions.solution: 20 cm is 5 groups of 4. So the length is 5 groups of 7, which is 35 centimeters.

questions.stem: Which list of pairs (red tiles, blue tiles) shows equivalent ratios?
questions.solution: In 2 to 3, 4 to 6 and 6 to 9, both numbers are multiplied by the same number each time (2, then 3). In the other lists the same number is added each time, which does not keep the ratio.

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of adult tickets to child tickets sold for a play is 4 to 9. The theater sold 36 child tickets. How many adult tickets did it sell?
questions.solution: 36 child tickets is 4 groups of 9. Each group goes with 4 adult tickets, so 4 x 4 = 16 adult tickets.

questions.stem: A tape diagram shows red paint as 5 equal parts and blue paint as 2 equal parts of the same size. Which is the ratio of blue paint to all the paint?
questions.solution: All the paint is 5 + 2 = 7 parts. Blue is 2 parts, so the ratio of blue paint to all the paint is 2 to 7.

questions.stem: A class has 9 girls and 12 boys. Which statement is true?
choices: The ratio of girls to all students is 3 to 4
The ratio of girls to boys is 3 to 4
The ratio of boys to girls is 3 to 4
The ratio of boys to all students is 3 to 4
questions.answer: The ratio of girls to boys is 3 to 4
questions.solution: The ratio of girls to boys is 9 to 12, which is 3 to 4 in simplest form. There are 21 students in all, so the ratio of girls to all students is 9 to 21, or 3 to 7. The ratio of boys to girls is 4 to 3, and boys to all students is 4 to 7.

solve.answer: The ratio of girls to boys is 3 to 4
solve.work: 9:12 = 3:4 girls to boys. Girls:all = 9:21=3:7; boys:all=12:21=4:7; boys:girls=4:3.

questions.stem: At a fair, the ratio of adults to children is 3 to 7. There are 56 more children than adults. How many people are at the fair in all?
questions.solution: The children have $7 - 3 = 4$ more parts than the adults, and those 4 parts are 56 people, so 1 part is 14 people. The fair has $3 + 7 = 10$ parts in all: $10 \times 14 = 140$ people.

solve.work: Children - adults = 7-3 = 4 parts = 56, so 1 part = 14. Total = 10 parts = 140. (42 adults, 98 children.)

questions.stem: Tia says that 15 to 24 is equivalent to 10 to 19 because she subtracted 5 from each number. Which is correct?
choices: Tia is right, because subtracting the same amount from both numbers keeps the ratio the same
Tia is right, because the two numbers in each ratio are 9 apart
Tia is wrong, because equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number
Tia is wrong, because the 5 should have been subtracted only from the 24
questions.answer: Tia is wrong, because equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number
questions.solution: Equivalent ratios are made by multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number. Subtracting 5 from each does not do that: 15 to 24 is 5 to 8 in simplest form, but 10 to 19 cannot be simplified. Keeping the same difference is not enough.

solve.answer: Tia is wrong, because equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number
solve.work: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying/dividing both by the same number; 15:24 = 5:8, 10:19 is not 5:8.

questions.stem: A ratio table lists cups of flour to cups of sugar for a cake: 6 to 4, then 9 to 6. At the same ratio, how many cups of flour go with 14 cups of sugar?
questions.solution: Both rows simplify to 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. 14 cups of sugar is 7 groups of 2, so the flour is $7 \times 3 = 21$ cups.

questions.stem: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 4 to 5. Which could be the total number of students in the class?
questions.solution: The students come in groups of $4 + 5 = 9$, so the total must be a multiple of 9. Of these, only 27 is ($3 \times 9$).

solve.work: Total must be a multiple of 4+5 = 9. 27 = 9*3 (12 boys, 15 girls). 30, 28, 32 are not multiples of 9.

questions.stem: The ratio of Jo's savings to Ben's savings is 3 to 5. Ben has 20 dollars more than Jo. How many dollars does Jo have?
questions.solution: Ben has $5 - 3 = 2$ more parts than Jo, and those 2 parts are 20 dollars, so 1 part is 10 dollars. Jo has 3 parts: $3 \times 10 = 30$ dollars.

questions.stem: A tape diagram shows 3 equal parts for Ana's money and 8 equal parts for Raj's money. Together they have 66 dollars. Which equation finds the value $p$ of one part?
questions.solution: Together there are $3 + 8 = 11$ equal parts, so $11p = 66$ and $p = 6$ dollars. Multiplying 3 by 8 or subtracting them gives the wrong number of parts.

questions.stem: The ratio of the length to the width of a rectangle is 5 to 3. The width is 12 centimeters. What is the length in centimeters?
questions.solution: 12 centimeters is 4 groups of 3, so the length is $4 \times 5 = 20$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Writing a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: Of 20 students, 8 chose soccer and the rest chose tennis. Which statement is true?
choices: The ratio of soccer to tennis is 2 to 5
The ratio of tennis to soccer is 2 to 3
The ratio of soccer to tennis is 2 to 3
The ratio of tennis to all students is 2 to 3
questions.answer: The ratio of soccer to tennis is 2 to 3
questions.solution: 12 students chose tennis. Soccer to tennis is 8 to 12, which is 2 to 3. The ratio 2 to 5 compares soccer to all the students, tennis to soccer is 3 to 2, and tennis to all the students is 3 to 5.

solve.answer: The ratio of soccer to tennis is 2 to 3
solve.work: Soccer 8, tennis 12. Soccer:tennis = 8:12 = 2:3 true. 2:5 false; tennis:all = 12:20 = 3:5 not 2:3; tennis:soccer = 3:2 not 2:3.

questions.stem: The ratio of Lee's marbles to Kai's marbles is 5 to 3. Lee gives 6 marbles to Kai, and then they have the same number. How many marbles did Lee have at first?
questions.solution: Lee has 2 more parts than Kai, and giving away 6 evens them out, so the 2 parts are $6 + 6 = 12$ marbles and 1 part is 6 marbles. Lee started with $5 \times 6 = 30$.

solve.work: Lee 5k, Kai 3k. 5k-6 = 3k+6 -> k = 6. Lee had 30 (Kai 18; both 24 after).

questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to 18 to 30 and has 21 as its first number?
questions.solution: 18 to 30 simplifies to 3 to 5. Multiplying by 7 gives 21 to 35. Adding 3 to both numbers gives 21 to 33, and the others do not keep the ratio.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: A recipe uses sugar and flour in the ratio 3 to 8. Tess used 24 cups of flour. Her friend used 5 more cups of sugar than Tess. How many cups of sugar did her friend use?
questions.solution: 24 cups of flour is 3 groups of 8, so Tess used 3 groups of 3 cups of sugar, which is 9 cups. Her friend used 9 + 5 = 14 cups.

solve.work: Tess: 3/8 = s/24 -> s = 9 cups sugar. Friend: 9 + 5 = 14.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: Tom runs 3 laps for every 2 laps Ben runs. Ben ran 14 laps. How many laps did they run together?
questions.solution: 14 laps is 7 groups of 2. So Tom ran 7 groups of 3, which is 21 laps. Together they ran 21 + 14 = 35 laps.

questions.stem: The first two rows of a ratio table of hours and dollars are 3 and 24, then 5 and 40. Which could be the next row?
questions.solution: The rate is 8 dollars for each hour (24 / 3 = 8 and 40 / 5 = 8). 8 hours go with 8 x 8 = 64 dollars.

questions.skill: Ratios as points on a graph
questions.stem: Each point (x, y) shows x gallons of paint and y rooms painted. The points (5, 2) and (10, 4) lie on a line through (0, 0). A point on this line has y equal to 14. What is its x?
questions.solution: The ratio of x to y is 5 to 2. y = 14 is 7 groups of 2, so x is 7 x 5 = 35.

questions.skill: Write a ratio from a situation
questions.stem: Which is the ratio of 2 hours to 30 minutes, written with both quantities in minutes?
questions.solution: 2 hours is 120 minutes, so the ratio is 120 to 30, which is 4 to 1. Both quantities must use the same unit.

questions.stem: Sasha says that 3 to 4 and 4 to 3 are equivalent ratios. Which statement is correct?
choices: They are not equivalent, because the order of the quantities changed
They are equivalent, because they use the same two numbers
They are equivalent, because both add up to 7
questions.answer: They are not equivalent, because the order of the quantities changed
questions.solution: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number, and 3 to 4 cannot become 4 to 3 that way. Reversing the order compares the quantities the other way around.

solve.answer: They are not equivalent, because the order of the quantities changed
solve.work: 3:4 compares first to second; 4:3 reverses; not equivalent.

questions.stem: Box A has 4 red marbles and 6 blue marbles. Box B has 10 red marbles and 15 blue marbles. All the marbles are poured into one bag. The ratio of red to blue marbles in the bag is 14 to ?. What is the ?
questions.solution: The bag has 4 + 10 = 14 red marbles and 6 + 15 = 21 blue marbles, so the ratio is 14 to 21.

questions.stem: A double number line has pairs of marks that line up at a steady ratio. The marks 6 and 15 line up. Which other two marks also line up?
questions.solution: 6 to 15 is 2 to 5. 10 to 25 is 5 groups of 2 to 5 groups of 5, so it is also 2 to 5. The others do not keep the ratio.

questions.stem: A tape diagram shows 5 equal parts for sneakers and 4 equal parts of the same size for sandals. There are 72 shoes in all. Which expression gives the number of shoes in one part?
questions.solution: There are 5 + 4 = 9 equal parts in all, so one part is 72 / 9 = 8 shoes.

solve.work: 9 equal parts in all: 72 / 9 = 8 shoes per part.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of cars to trucks in a lot is 7 to 2. Which could NOT be the total number of vehicles?
questions.solution: Each group of 7 cars and 2 trucks has 9 vehicles, so the total must be a multiple of 9. 27, 45 and 54 are multiples of 9, but 50 is not.

solve.work: 7:2 gives totals that are multiples of 9. 54=9*6, 45=9*5, 27=9*3; 50 is not a multiple of 9.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: A school wants 1 teacher for every 15 students. It has 480 students and 12 teachers. How many more teachers does it need?
questions.solution: 480 / 15 = 32 teachers are needed. It has 12, so it needs 32 - 12 = 20 more teachers.

questions.stem: Which pair of mixes has the same ratio of juice to water?
choices: A: 3 juice, 5 water; B: 9 juice, 15 water
A: 3 juice, 5 water; B: 6 juice, 8 water
A: 3 juice, 5 water; B: 5 juice, 3 water
A: 3 juice, 5 water; B: 9 juice, 20 water
questions.answer: A: 3 juice, 5 water; B: 9 juice, 15 water
questions.solution: Multiplying 3 and 5 by 3 gives 9 and 15, so mix B has the same ratio as mix A. In the others the numbers were added to, reversed, or not scaled together.

solve.answer: A: 3 juice, 5 water; B: 9 juice, 15 water

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: A bakery sold muffins and bagels in the ratio 5 to 3. It sold 18 fewer bagels than muffins. How many muffins and bagels did it sell in all?
questions.solution: The difference of 5 - 3 = 2 parts is 18 items, so 1 part is 9 items. In all there are 5 + 3 = 8 parts, and 8 x 9 = 72 items.

solve.work: Difference is 5-3 = 2 parts = 18, so 1 part = 9. Total 8 parts = 72 (45 muffins, 27 bagels).

questions.skill: Find a missing quantity from a ratio
questions.stem: A garden has 12 tomato plants and 20 pepper plants. Another garden has the same ratio of tomato plants to pepper plants and has 21 tomato plants. How many pepper plants does it have?
questions.solution: 12 to 20 is 3 to 5 in simplest form. 21 tomato plants is 7 groups of 3, so there are 7 x 5 = 35 pepper plants.

questions.stem: A tape diagram shows 3 equal parts for Mia's books and 5 equal parts of the same size for Leo's books. Leo has 10 more books than Mia. Which equation finds the number of books $p$ in one part?
questions.solution: Leo has 5 - 3 = 2 more parts than Mia, and that is 10 books, so 2p = 10 and p = 5.

solve.work: Leo 5 parts minus Mia 3 parts = 2 parts = 10, so 2p = 10.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of the length to the width of a flag is 3 to 2. The perimeter of the flag is 60 centimeters. What is its length in centimeters?
questions.solution: One length and one width make 3 + 2 = 5 parts, and the perimeter is 2 lengths and 2 widths, which is 10 parts. 60 / 10 = 6 centimeters in a part. The length is 3 parts, so 3 x 6 = 18 centimeters.

questions.stem: Mia has 8 red beads and 12 blue beads. She adds more of each color so the ratio of red to blue stays the same. Which could be her new totals?
questions.solution: 8 to 12 is 2 to 3. 14 to 21 is 7 groups of 2 to 7 groups of 3, so it is also 2 to 3. For the other options, the ratio is not 2 to 3 (for example 14 to 18 is 7 to 9).

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: A paint mix uses 3 parts blue to 5 parts white. Lila has 12 cups of blue paint and 25 cups of white paint. What is the greatest number of cups of mix she can make using this ratio?
questions.solution: The 25 cups of white would need 15 cups of blue, but she has only 12. So the blue paint limits her. 12 cups of blue is 4 groups of 3, which goes with 4 x 5 = 20 cups of white. In all, 12 + 20 = 32 cups.

solve.work: Blue limits: 12/3 = 4 batches (white needs 20 <= 25). 4 x (3+5) = 32 cups.

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 to 8 and their sum is 91. What is the greater number?
questions.solution: There are 5 + 8 = 13 parts. 91 / 13 = 7 in each part. The greater number is 8 parts, so 8 x 7 = 56.

questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to 1.5 to 2.5?
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 2: 1.5 x 2 = 3 and 2.5 x 2 = 5. The ratio is 3 to 5.

questions.stem: Which does NOT describe a ratio of red cars to blue cars of 2 to 3?
choices: For every 2 red cars there are 3 blue cars
questions.solution: If 2 of every 3 cars are red, the other 1 is blue, so the ratio of red to blue is 2 to 1. The other options are all 2 to 3.

solve.work: '2 of every 3 cars are red' is part-to-whole: red:blue would be 2:1, not 2:3. The others are 2:3 (6:9 and 10:15 are equivalent).

questions.skill: Parts, totals and differences of a ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of afternoon tickets to evening tickets sold for a show is 5 to 8. In all, 104 tickets were sold. How many more evening tickets than afternoon tickets were sold?
questions.solution: There are 5 + 8 = 13 parts. 104 / 13 = 8 tickets in each part. Evening has 8 - 5 = 3 more parts, so 3 x 8 = 24 more tickets.

solve.work: 5 + 8 = 13 parts, 104/13 = 8 per part. Evening 64, afternoon 40, difference 24.

questions.stem: A ratio table has these rows: 6 and 15, then 10 and ?, then 14 and 35. What number replaces the ?
questions.solution: 6 to 15 is 2 to 5. 10 is 5 groups of 2, so the missing number is 5 x 5 = 25. Check: 14 to 35 is 7 groups of 2 to 7 groups of 5.

questions.stem: A car travels 240 miles in 4 hours at a steady speed. How many miles does it travel in 1 hour?
questions.solution: Divide the miles by the hours: 240 / 4 = 60. The car travels 60 miles in 1 hour.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to $8:4$ and has 1 as its second number?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 4: $8 \div 4 = 2$ and $4 \div 4 = 1$. The ratio is $2:1$.

questions.stem: Five pencils cost 10 dollars. How many dollars does 1 pencil cost?
questions.solution: Divide the cost by the number of pencils: 10 / 5 = 2. One pencil costs 2 dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret a unit rate in context
questions.stem: A runner runs 3 miles in 24 minutes. The unit rate is 8 minutes per mile. What does that unit rate mean?
choices: The runner runs 8 miles in each minute.
The runner takes 8 minutes to run each mile.
The runner takes 24 minutes to run each mile.
The runner runs 3 miles in each 8 minutes.
questions.answer: The runner takes 8 minutes to run each mile.
questions.solution: Per mile means for each 1 mile. 24 minutes / 3 miles = 8 minutes for each mile, so the runner takes 8 minutes to run each mile.

solve.answer: The runner takes 8 minutes to run each mile.
solve.work: 24 / 3 = 8 minutes per mile: 8 minutes for each mile.

questions.stem: A tap fills 30 liters of water in 5 minutes. How many liters does it fill in 1 minute?
questions.solution: Divide the liters by the minutes: 30 / 5 = 6. The tap fills 6 liters in 1 minute.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: For every 12 boys in a club there are 3 girls. Which statement gives this ratio for 1 girl?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 3: 12 / 3 = 4 boys and 3 / 3 = 1 girl. There are 4 boys for every 1 girl.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: For every 15 red beads in a necklace there are 5 blue beads. How many red beads are there for each blue bead?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 5: 15 / 5 = 3 red beads for each 5 / 5 = 1 blue bead. The answer is 3.

questions.skill: Interpret a unit rate in context
questions.stem: A worker earns 90 dollars in 6 hours. Which sentence gives the unit rate in dollars per hour?
choices: The worker works 15 hours for each dollar.
The worker earns 84 dollars each hour.
The worker earns 15 dollars each hour.
The worker earns 540 dollars each hour.
questions.answer: The worker earns 15 dollars each hour.
questions.solution: Divide the dollars by the hours: 90 / 6 = 15. The worker earns 15 dollars each hour.

solve.answer: The worker earns 15 dollars each hour.

questions.stem: Store A sells 3 oranges for 6 dollars. Store B sells 5 oranges for 15 dollars. How many more dollars does one orange cost at Store B than at Store A?
questions.solution: At Store A one orange costs 6 / 3 = 2 dollars. At Store B one orange costs 15 / 5 = 3 dollars. The difference is 3 - 2 = 1 dollar.

questions.skill: Interpret a unit rate in context
questions.stem: At a school the ratio of students to teachers is 20 to 1. Which statement is true?
choices: There are 20 students for each teacher.
There are 20 teachers for each student.
There are 21 students for each teacher.
There are 20 students in the whole school.
questions.answer: There are 20 students for each teacher.
questions.solution: A ratio of students to teachers of 20 to 1 means 20 students for every 1 teacher.

solve.answer: There are 20 students for each teacher.
solve.work: 20 to 1 means 20 students for each teacher.

questions.skill: Find both unit rates of a ratio
questions.stem: A turtle walks 10 feet in 5 minutes. Which pair gives both unit rates?
choices: 0.5 foot per minute and 2 minutes per foot
5 feet per minute and 2 minutes per foot
2 feet per minute and 0.5 minute per foot
2 feet per minute and 2 minutes per foot
questions.answer: 2 feet per minute and 0.5 minute per foot
questions.solution: $10 \div 5 = 2$ feet per minute, and $5 \div 10 = 0.5$ minute per foot.

solve.answer: 2 feet per minute and 0.5 minute per foot
solve.work: 10/5 = 2 ft per minute; 5/10 = 0.5 minute per foot.

questions.skill: Interpret a unit rate in context
questions.stem: Which situation has a unit rate of 6 miles per hour?
questions.solution: $18 \div 3 = 6$ miles per hour. The others give 4, $\frac{1}{6}$ and 2 miles per hour.

questions.stem: Mina reads 6 pages in 2 minutes. Sam reads 5 pages in 1 minute. How many more pages per minute does Sam read than Mina?
questions.solution: Mina reads $6 \div 2 = 3$ pages per minute. Sam reads 5 pages per minute. The difference is $5 - 3 = 2$.

questions.skill: Use a unit rate to find an amount
questions.stem: A recipe uses 4 cups of water for every 1 cup of rice. How many cups of water are needed for 3 cups of rice?
questions.solution: The unit ratio is 4 cups of water to 1 cup of rice, so 3 cups of rice need $4 \times 3 = 12$ cups of water.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: A trail mix has 10 cups of raisins for every 5 cups of nuts. Written with 1 cup of nuts, the ratio is ? cups of raisins to 1 cup of nuts. What is the ?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 5: 10 to 5 is the same as 2 to 1, so the ? is 2.

questions.skill: Use a unit rate to find an amount
questions.stem: A car uses 1 gallon of gas for every 25 miles. How many gallons does it use to go 100 miles?
questions.solution: Each 25 miles uses 1 gallon, so 100 miles uses $100 \div 25 = 4$ gallons.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of cats to dogs at a shelter is 14 to 2. The same ratio can be written ? to 1. What is the ?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 2: 14 to 2 is the same as 7 to 1, so the ? is 7.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: Which ratio is equivalent to $5:15$ and has 1 as its first number?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 5: $5:15$ is the same as $1:3$.

questions.skill: Interpret a unit rate in context
questions.stem: A faucet drips 10 milliliters of water in 5 seconds. Which statement is true?
choices: It drips 2 milliliters in each second.
It drips 5 milliliters in each second.
It drips 10 milliliters in each second.
It takes 2 seconds to drip each milliliter.
questions.answer: It drips 2 milliliters in each second.
questions.solution: $10 \div 5 = 2$, so it drips 2 milliliters in each second.

solve.answer: It drips 2 milliliters in each second.
solve.work: 10/5 = 2 mL per second (and 0.5 s per mL, so the first is false).

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: A drink uses 1 cup of syrup for every 4 cups of water. Which statement is true?
choices: There are 4 cups of water for each cup of syrup.
There are 4 cups of syrup for each cup of water.
There are 5 cups of water for each cup of syrup.
There is 1 cup of water for each 4 cups of syrup.
questions.answer: There are 4 cups of water for each cup of syrup.
questions.solution: The ratio of syrup to water is 1 to 4, so each cup of syrup goes with 4 cups of water.

solve.answer: There are 4 cups of water for each cup of syrup.
solve.work: 1 syrup : 4 water means 4 cups of water for each cup of syrup.

questions.stem: A worker packs 20 boxes in 4 hours at a steady rate. Which gives the unit rate?
questions.solution: $20 \div 4 = 5$, so the worker packs 5 boxes per hour.

questions.stem: A pack of 4 batteries costs 12 dollars. How many dollars does 1 battery cost?
questions.solution: Divide the cost by the number of batteries: $12 \div 4 = 3$ dollars.

questions.stem: A bakery puts 48 rolls into 6 boxes, with the same number of rolls in each box. How many rolls are in 1 box?
questions.solution: Divide the rolls by the boxes: $48 \div 6 = 8$ rolls in 1 box.

questions.stem: Shop A sells 4 notebooks for 8 dollars. Shop B sells 3 notebooks for 9 dollars. Which shop charges less for 1 notebook?
questions.solution: Shop A: $8 \div 4 = 2$ dollars. Shop B: $9 \div 3 = 3$ dollars. Shop A is less.

solve.work: A: 8/4 = 2 dollars each. B: 9/3 = 3 dollars each. A is less.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: The ratio of red marbles to blue marbles is 18 to 6. Which statement gives this ratio for 1 blue marble?
choices: 12 red marbles for every 1 blue marble.
3 red marbles for every 1 blue marble.
6 red marbles for every 1 blue marble.
1 red marble for every 3 blue marbles.
questions.answer: 3 red marbles for every 1 blue marble.
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 6: 18 to 6 is 3 to 1, so there are 3 red marbles for every 1 blue marble.

solve.answer: 3 red marbles for every 1 blue marble.

questions.stem: A garden hose fills a bucket with 63 liters of water in 7 minutes at a steady rate. How many liters does it fill in 1 minute?
questions.solution: Divide the liters by the minutes: $63 \div 7 = 9$ liters in 1 minute.

questions.stem: A box of 12 pencils costs 3 dollars. How many dollars does 1 pencil cost?
questions.solution: Divide the cost by the number of pencils: $3 \div 12 = 0.25$ dollar.

questions.stem: Five tickets cost 45 dollars in all. How many dollars does 1 ticket cost?
questions.solution: Divide the cost by the number of tickets: $45 \div 5 = 9$ dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret a unit rate in context
questions.stem: A cyclist rides 30 miles in 2 hours, which is a unit rate of 15 miles per hour. What does this unit rate mean?
choices: The cyclist rides 15 miles in each hour.
The cyclist rides 15 hours for each mile.
The cyclist rides 2 miles in each hour.
The cyclist rides 30 miles in each hour.
questions.answer: The cyclist rides 15 miles in each hour.
questions.solution: A rate of 15 miles per hour means 15 miles for each 1 hour: $30 \div 2 = 15$.

solve.answer: The cyclist rides 15 miles in each hour.
solve.work: 15 miles per hour means 15 miles in each hour.

questions.stem: Leo rides his bike 36 miles in 3 hours at a steady speed. How many miles does he ride in 1 hour?
questions.solution: Divide the distance by the time: $36 \div 3 = 12$ miles in 1 hour.

questions.skill: Find both unit rates of a ratio
questions.stem: A baker uses 6 cups of flour to make 12 muffins. How many cups of flour does 1 muffin need?
questions.solution: Divide the cups by the muffins: $6 \div 12 = 0.5$ cup for 1 muffin.

questions.stem: A printer prints 40 pages in 8 minutes at a steady rate. How many pages does it print in 1 minute?
questions.solution: The unit rate is $40 \div 8 = 5$ pages per minute.

questions.stem: For every 8 sandwiches, a cafe uses 2 loaves of bread. Which is a unit ratio of sandwiches to loaves?
questions.solution: Divide both numbers by 2: 8 sandwiches to 2 loaves is the same as 4 sandwiches to 1 loaf. The second number must be 1 for a unit ratio of sandwiches to loaves.

questions.stem: Twelve muffins cost 9 dollars. How many dollars does 1 muffin cost?
questions.solution: Divide the cost by the number of muffins: 9 / 12 = 0.75. One muffin costs 0.75 dollars (75 cents).

questions.skill: Find both unit rates of a ratio
questions.stem: A hose fills 4 gallons in 10 minutes. Which pair gives both unit rates?
choices: 2.5 gallons per minute and 0.4 minute per gallon
6 gallons per minute and 14 minutes per gallon
0.4 gallon per minute and 2.5 minutes per gallon
40 gallons per minute and 0.025 minute per gallon
questions.answer: 0.4 gallon per minute and 2.5 minutes per gallon
questions.solution: Gallons per minute: 4 / 10 = 0.4. Minutes per gallon: 10 / 4 = 2.5. Both unit rates are 0.4 gallon per minute and 2.5 minutes per gallon.

solve.answer: 0.4 gallon per minute and 2.5 minutes per gallon
solve.work: 4 / 10 = 0.4 gallon per minute; 10 / 4 = 2.5 minutes per gallon.

questions.skill: Find both unit rates of a ratio
questions.stem: A snail crawls 6 feet in 30 minutes. How many minutes does it take the snail to crawl 1 foot?
questions.solution: Divide the minutes by the feet: 30 / 6 = 5. It takes 5 minutes for each foot.

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: Which ratio is NOT equivalent to $18:6$?
questions.solution: Divide $18:6$ by 6 to get $3:1$. Then $9:3$ and $6:2$ also equal $3:1$. The ratio $1:3$ has the numbers in the other order, so it is not equivalent.

questions.stem: Five tickets cost 42.50 dollars. How many dollars does 1 ticket cost?
questions.solution: Divide the cost by the number of tickets: 42.50 / 5 = 8.50. One ticket costs 8.50 dollars.

questions.stem: Brand A sells 6 cans for 4.50 dollars. Brand B sells 8 cans for 5.60 dollars. Which brand costs less per can?
choices: Brand A, at 0.75 dollars per can.
Brand B, at 0.70 dollars per can.
Brand B, at 0.75 dollars per can.
Brand A, at 0.70 dollars per can.
questions.answer: Brand B, at 0.70 dollars per can.
questions.solution: Brand A: 4.50 / 6 = 0.75 dollars per can. Brand B: 5.60 / 8 = 0.70 dollars per can. Brand B costs less per can.

solve.answer: Brand B, at 0.70 dollars per can.

questions.skill: Use a unit rate to find an amount
questions.stem: A pool drains 90 gallons in 12 minutes at a steady rate. How many gallons drain in 5 minutes?
questions.solution: Unit rate: 90 / 12 = 7.5 gallons in 1 minute. In 5 minutes: 7.5 x 5 = 37.5 gallons.

questions.skill: Interpret a unit rate in context
questions.stem: A car uses 5 gallons of gas to travel 150 miles. Which statement is correct?
choices: The car uses 30 gallons for each mile.
The car goes $\frac{1}{30}$ mile on each gallon.
The car uses $\frac{1}{30}$ gallon for each mile.
The car uses $\frac{1}{5}$ gallon for each mile.
questions.answer: The car uses $\frac{1}{30}$ gallon for each mile.
questions.solution: Gallons for each mile: 5 / 150 = 1/30. So the car uses 1/30 gallon for each mile. (It also goes 150 / 5 = 30 miles on each gallon.)

solve.answer: The car uses $\frac{1}{30}$ gallon for each mile.
solve.work: 5 / 150 = 1/30 gallon per mile (and 30 miles per gallon).

questions.skill: Write a ratio as an equivalent unit ratio
questions.stem: In a drink, 3 cups of juice are mixed with 12 cups of water. How many cups of water are there for each cup of juice?
questions.solution: Divide both amounts by 3: 12 / 3 = 4 cups of water for each 3 / 3 = 1 cup of juice.

solve.work: 12 / 3 = 4 cups of water per cup of juice.

questions.stem: Tia reads 30 pages in 40 minutes. How many pages does she read in 1 minute?
