questions.solution: In $y = 6x$ the number $x$ is multiplied by 6, like $x$ bags of 6 marbles each.

solve.answer: Each bag holds 6 marbles, and $x$ bags hold $y$ marbles in all
solve.work: 6 per bag times x bags = y: y = 6x. Others are 6/x, 6+x, x-6.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area of a triangle = $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30$ square centimeters.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 8 meters and a height of 5 meters. What is its area in square meters?
questions.solution: Area of a parallelogram = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 square meters.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 12 inches and a height of 7 inches. Which expression gives its area in square inches?
questions.solution: A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height, so its area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 7$. Leaving out the half gives the rectangle’s area, and adding the lengths does not give an area.

solve.work: Area = 1/2 x base x height = 1/2 x 12 x 7.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 9 feet and 4 feet. What is its area in square feet?
questions.solution: In a right triangle, the two legs are the base and the height. Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 4 = 18$ square feet.

solve.work: Legs are base and height: 1/2 x 9 x 4 = 18.

questions.skill: Compose and decompose triangles and rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle is 6 units long and 8 units wide. It is cut along a diagonal into two identical triangles. What is the area of each triangle in square units?
questions.solution: The rectangle has area 6 × 8 = 48 square units. Two identical triangles share it equally, so each has 48 ÷ 2 = 24 square units.

questions.skill: Area of a polygon made of parts
questions.stem: An L-shaped figure is made of two rectangles that do not overlap. One is 6 units by 4 units and the other is 3 units by 2 units. What is the area of the figure in square units?
questions.solution: Add the areas of the two rectangles: 6 × 4 = 24 and 3 × 2 = 6. Then 24 + 6 = 30 square units.

questions.skill: Compose and decompose triangles and rectangles
questions.stem: A triangle and a rectangle have the same base and the same height. How does the triangle’s area compare with the rectangle’s area?
choices: It is one fourth as large.
questions.solution: A triangle fills exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

solve.work: Triangle area = 1/2 bh, rectangle = bh: half as large.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 10 centimeters, a slanted side of 7 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. Which two lengths should be multiplied to find its area?
questions.solution: Area of a parallelogram = base × height. The base is 10 and the height is 6, so multiply 10 and 6. The slanted side is not used.

solve.work: Area = base x height = 10 x 6; the slanted side is not used.

questions.skill: Compose and decompose triangles and rectangles
questions.stem: Two identical triangles, each with a base of 6 inches and a height of 4 inches, are put together to make a parallelogram. What is the area of the parallelogram in square inches?
questions.solution: Each triangle has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$ square inches. Two triangles make 24 square inches.

solve.work: Each triangle 1/2 x 6 x 4 = 12; two make 24.

questions.skill: Area of a polygon made of parts
questions.stem: A figure is made of a rectangle 8 units wide and 3 units tall, with a triangle on top of it. The triangle has a base of 8 units (the top of the rectangle) and a height of 3 units. What is the area of the whole figure in square units?
questions.solution: Rectangle: 8 × 3 = 24. Triangle: $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 3 = 12$. Total: 24 + 12 = 36 square units.

solve.work: Rectangle 8 x 3 = 24; triangle 1/2 x 8 x 3 = 12; total 36.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 7.5 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times 7.5 \times 4 = 15$ square centimeters.

questions.stem: A right triangle has sides of 5 centimeters, 12 centimeters and 13 centimeters. The 13-centimeter side is the longest. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The two shorter sides, 5 and 12, meet at the square corner, so they are the base and the height. Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30$. Using 13 as a side gives a wrong answer.

questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 9 centimeters, a height of 6 centimeters and a slanted side of 7 centimeters. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = base × height = 9 × 6 = 54 square centimeters. The slanted side is not part of the formula.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 4 centimeters and 10 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. It is cut into a rectangle that is 4 centimeters by 5 centimeters and two identical right triangles, each with legs of 3 centimeters and 5 centimeters. What is the area of the trapezoid in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Rectangle: 4 × 5 = 20. Each triangle: $\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 5 = 7.5$, so two triangles are 15. Total: 20 + 15 = 35 square centimeters.

solve.work: Rectangle 4 x 5 = 20; each triangle 1/2 x 3 x 5 = 7.5, two = 15; total 35. Check (4+10)/2 x 5 = 35.

questions.skill: Area of a polygon with a piece removed
questions.stem: A rectangle is 10 units long and 8 units wide. A rectangle 4 units by 3 units is cut out of one corner. What is the area of the remaining shape in square units?
questions.solution: Whole rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80. Piece cut out: 4 × 3 = 12. Remaining: 80 − 12 = 68 square units.

questions.stem: A garden shaped like a parallelogram has a base of 5.5 meters and a height of 4 meters. What is the area of the garden in square meters?
questions.solution: Area = base × height = 5.5 × 4 = 22 square meters.

questions.stem: A triangular wall has a base of 4 meters and a height of 3 meters. One can of paint covers 3 square meters. How many cans are needed to cover the wall once?
questions.solution: Area of the wall = $\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3 = 6$ square meters. Each can covers 3 square meters, so 6 ÷ 3 = 2 cans.

questions.skill: Compose and decompose triangles and rectangles
questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 8 units and a height of 6 units. Which shape has the same area as the triangle?
choices: A parallelogram with base 8 units and height 6 units
questions.solution: The triangle has area $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6 = 24$. A 4 by 6 rectangle has area 24. The 8 by 6 rectangle and the parallelogram each have area 48, and the 4 by 3 rectangle has area 12.

questions.skill: Area of a polygon with a piece removed
questions.stem: A square tile is 10 centimeters on each side. A triangle with a base of 10 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters is painted blue. What is the area of the tile that is not blue, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Tile: 10 × 10 = 100. Blue triangle: $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 4 = 20$. Not blue: 100 − 20 = 80 square centimeters.

solve.work: Tile 100; blue 1/2 x 10 x 4 = 20; not blue 80.

questions.skill: Area of a polygon made of parts
questions.stem: A rectangle is 6 units wide and 5 units tall. A right triangle with legs of 6 units and 8 units is attached along the rectangle’s bottom edge, so the 6-unit leg lies along that edge. Which expression gives the area of the whole shape?
questions.solution: Rectangle: 6 × 5. Triangle: half of base times height, with base 6 and height 8, so $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8$. Add the two areas.

solve.work: Rectangle 6 x 5; triangle 1/2 x 6 x 8; total 6 x 5 + 1/2 x 6 x 8.

questions.skill: Missing base or height from the area
questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 36 square centimeters and a base of 9 centimeters. What is its height in centimeters?
questions.solution: Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times h = 36$, so 9 × h = 72 and h = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing base or height from the area
questions.stem: A parallelogram has an area of 91 square meters and a height of 7 meters. What is its base in meters?
questions.solution: Area = base × height, so base = 91 ÷ 7 = 13 meters.

questions.stem: A rhombus has diagonals of 10 centimeters and 8 centimeters. The diagonals cross at right angles at their midpoints and cut the rhombus into four identical right triangles. What is the area of the rhombus in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each diagonal is cut in half, so each small right triangle has legs 5 and 4. Its area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4 = 10$. Four of them make 40 square centimeters.

solve.work: Each triangle has legs 5 and 4: area 10; four make 40. (10 x 8 / 2 = 40.)

questions.stem: A diagonal cuts a trapezoid into two triangles. One triangle has a base of 7 centimeters (the shorter parallel side) and the other has a base of 13 centimeters (the longer parallel side). Both triangles have the same height. The trapezoid has an area of 80 square centimeters. What is the height in centimeters?
questions.solution: The areas add: $\frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times h + \frac{1}{2} \times 13 \times h = \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times h = 10h$. So 10h = 80 and h = 8 centimeters.

questions.skill: Area of a polygon with a piece removed
questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 15 meters long and 10 meters wide. Inside it, not overlapping, are a triangular flower bed with a base of 6 meters and a height of 5 meters, and a square pond 3 meters on each side. The rest is grass. What is the area of the grass in square meters?
questions.solution: Garden: 15 × 10 = 150. Flower bed: $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 5 = 15$. Pond: 3 × 3 = 9. Grass: 150 − 15 − 9 = 126 square meters.

solve.work: Garden 150; bed 1/2 x 6 x 5 = 15; pond 9; grass 150 - 24 = 126.

questions.stem: Triangle X has a base of 10 units and a height of 6 units. Triangle Y has a base of 5 units and a height of 12 units. Which statement is true?
choices: Triangle X has the larger area.
Both have an area of 30 square units.
Triangle Y has the larger area.
Both have an area of 60 square units.
questions.answer: Both have an area of 30 square units.
questions.solution: Triangle X: $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30$. Triangle Y: $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30$. The areas are equal. 60 would be the area of a rectangle with those lengths.

solve.answer: Both have an area of 30 square units.

questions.skill: Missing base or height from the area
questions.stem: A parallelogram has a base of 14 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. A triangle has the same area as the parallelogram and a base of 12 centimeters. What is the height of the triangle in centimeters?
questions.solution: Parallelogram: 14 × 6 = 84. Triangle: $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times h = 84$, so 6h = 84 and h = 14 centimeters.

solve.work: Parallelogram 14 x 6 = 84; 1/2 x 12 x h = 84, h = 14.

questions.stem: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 5 units and 9 units and a height of 4 units. A diagonal cuts it into two triangles that have those parallel sides as bases. Which expression gives the area of the trapezoid?
questions.solution: Each triangle has half of its base times the height 4: $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4$ and $\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 4$. The trapezoid’s area is the sum.

solve.work: Two triangles: 1/2 x 5 x 4 + 1/2 x 9 x 4 = 28.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 2.5 meters and a height of 3.2 meters. What is its area in square meters?
questions.solution: Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times 2.5 \times 3.2 = \frac{8}{2} = 4$ square meters.

questions.skill: Compose and decompose triangles and rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle is 16 centimeters long and 9 centimeters wide. A point is marked on one long side and joined by straight segments to the two ends of the opposite long side, making a triangle. What is the area of the triangle in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The triangle’s base is the opposite long side, 16 centimeters, and its height is the width of the rectangle, 9 centimeters, wherever the point is. Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 9 = 72$.

solve.work: Triangle base 16 (the opposite long side), height 9 (width): 1/2 x 16 x 9 = 72.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism from its fractional edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 2 cm long, $\frac{1}{2}$ cm wide and 3 cm high. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume = length $\times$ width $\times$ height $= 2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 3 = 3$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism from its fractional edges
questions.stem: A small box is $\frac{1}{2}$ inch long, $\frac{1}{3}$ inch wide and $\frac{1}{5}$ inch high. What is its volume?
questions.solution: Multiply the three edges: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{30}$ cubic inch.

questions.skill: Fill a prism with unit cubes of fractional edge
questions.stem: A cube with edges of 1 unit is filled with small cubes whose edges are $\frac{1}{2}$ unit. How many small cubes does it take?
questions.solution: Each edge of the big cube holds 2 small cubes, so the number is $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$.

questions.skill: Volume as base area times height
questions.stem: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of $\frac{3}{4}$ square foot. The prism is 4 feet high. What is its volume in cubic feet?
questions.solution: Volume = base area $\times$ height $= \frac{3}{4} \times 4 = 3$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Find a missing edge from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of 3 cubic feet. Its base has an area of 6 square feet. How many feet high is the prism?
questions.solution: Volume = base area $\times$ height, so height = volume $\div$ base area $= 3 \div 6 = \frac{1}{2}$ foot.

questions.skill: Solve a volume problem in context
questions.stem: A prism has length $\frac{1}{2}$ m, width $\frac{3}{4}$ m and height 5 m. Which expression gives its volume in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Volume is length $\times$ width $\times$ height, so the expression is $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times 5$.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism from its fractional edges
questions.stem: A gift box is $\frac{1}{2}$ foot long, $\frac{1}{2}$ foot wide and 3 feet tall. What is its volume in cubic feet?
questions.solution: Multiply the edges: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times 3 = \frac{3}{4}$ cubic foot.

questions.skill: Fill a prism with unit cubes of fractional edge
questions.stem: Jada fills a prism that is 1 unit long, 1 unit wide and $\frac{1}{2}$ unit high with cubes whose edges are $\frac{1}{2}$ unit. How many cubes does she use?
questions.solution: Along the length there are 2 cubes, along the width 2 cubes and along the height 1 cube: $2 \times 2 \times 1 = 4$ cubes.

questions.stem: A prism has edges of $\frac{1}{2}$ meter, $\frac{1}{4}$ meter and 2 meters. Its volume is $\frac{1}{4}$ of what unit?
questions.solution: Volume measures the space inside a solid, so it is in cubic units. With edges in meters, the volume is in cubic meters: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times 2 = \frac{1}{4}$ cubic meter.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism from its fractional edges
questions.stem: A block is $\frac{1}{3}$ foot long, $\frac{1}{3}$ foot wide and 3 feet tall. What is its volume?
questions.solution: Multiply the edges: $\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{3} \times 3 = \frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}$ cubic foot.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism from its fractional edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is $\frac{3}{2}$ cm long, $\frac{2}{3}$ cm wide and $\frac{5}{4}$ cm high. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Multiply: $\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} = 1$, and $1 \times \frac{5}{4} = \frac{5}{4}$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism from its fractional edges
questions.stem: A planter is $\frac{5}{2}$ feet long, $\frac{1}{2}$ foot wide and $\frac{1}{2}$ foot deep. How many cubic feet of soil does it hold when full?
questions.solution: Volume $= \frac{5}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{8}$ cubic foot.

questions.skill: Find a missing edge from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of $\frac{3}{4}$ cubic foot. It is $\frac{3}{2}$ feet long and $\frac{1}{4}$ foot wide. How many feet high is it?
questions.solution: The base area is $\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{8}$ square foot. Height = volume $\div$ base area $= \frac{3}{4} \div \frac{3}{8} = 2$ feet.

questions.skill: Volume as base area times height
questions.stem: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of $\frac{5}{6}$ square meter, and the prism is $\frac{3}{10}$ meter high. What is its volume?
questions.solution: Volume = base area $\times$ height $= \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{3}{10} = \frac{15}{60} = \frac{1}{4}$ cubic meter.

questions.skill: Fill a prism with unit cubes of fractional edge
questions.stem: A prism is 2 feet long, 1 foot wide and $\frac{2}{3}$ foot high. It is packed with cubes whose edges are $\frac{1}{3}$ foot. How many cubes fill it?
questions.solution: Along the length there are $2 \div \frac{1}{3} = 6$ cubes, along the width $1 \div \frac{1}{3} = 3$ cubes and along the height $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{3} = 2$ cubes. That is $6 \times 3 \times 2 = 36$ cubes.

questions.skill: Solve a volume problem in context
questions.stem: A tank is 2 feet long, $\frac{3}{4}$ foot wide and 1 foot tall. It is filled with water to $\frac{2}{3}$ of its volume. How much water is in the tank?
questions.solution: The tank holds $2 \times \frac{3}{4} \times 1 = \frac{3}{2}$ cubic feet. Two thirds of that is $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{2} = 1$ cubic foot.

questions.skill: Find a missing edge from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of 6 cubic units. Its length is 4 units and its width is $\frac{3}{2}$ units. Which expression gives its height?
questions.solution: Volume = length $\times$ width $\times$ height, so height = volume $\div$ (length $\times$ width) $= 6 \div \left( 4 \times \frac{3}{2} \right) = 1$ unit.

questions.skill: Solve a volume problem in context
questions.stem: A bag of soil fills $\frac{1}{2}$ cubic foot. How many bags are needed to fill a planter box that is 2 feet long, 1 foot wide and $\frac{3}{2}$ feet tall?
questions.solution: The box holds $2 \times 1 \times \frac{3}{2} = 3$ cubic feet. Each bag fills $\frac{1}{2}$ cubic foot, so $3 \div \frac{1}{2} = 6$ bags are needed.

questions.skill: Fill a prism with unit cubes of fractional edge
questions.stem: A box is 3 inches long, 2 inches wide and 1 inch tall. How many cubes with edges of $\frac{1}{2}$ inch does it take to fill it?
questions.solution: Each inch holds 2 cubes along an edge, so the box takes $6 \times 4 \times 2 = 48$ cubes. (Each small cube has volume $\frac{1}{8}$ cubic inch, and $6 \div \frac{1}{8} = 48$.)

questions.skill: Volume as base area times height
questions.stem: The rectangular base of a prism measures $\frac{3}{4}$ m by $\frac{2}{3}$ m. The prism is 6 m tall. What is its volume in cubic meters?
questions.solution: The base area is $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{2}$ square meter. Volume = base area $\times$ height $= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3$ cubic meters.

questions.skill: Volume of a prism from its fractional edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is $2\frac{1}{2}$ feet long, $1\frac{1}{2}$ feet wide and $\frac{2}{3}$ foot high. What is its volume in cubic feet?
questions.solution: Write the mixed numbers as fractions: $\frac{5}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{30}{12} = \frac{5}{2}$, or $2\frac{1}{2}$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Find a missing edge from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of $7\frac{1}{2}$ cubic centimeters. Its length is $2\frac{1}{2}$ cm and its width is $1\frac{1}{2}$ cm. How many centimeters high is it?
questions.solution: The base area is $\frac{5}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{15}{4}$ square cm. Height = $\frac{15}{2} \div \frac{15}{4} = 2$ cm.

questions.skill: Solve a volume problem in context
questions.stem: A tank is 4 feet long, $\frac{3}{2}$ feet wide and $\frac{5}{2}$ feet tall. Water fills it to $\frac{3}{5}$ of its height. How much water is in the tank?
questions.solution: The water is $\frac{3}{5} \times \frac{5}{2} = \frac{3}{2}$ feet deep. Its volume is $4 \times \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} = 9$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Solve a volume problem in context
questions.stem: A toy block is made by joining two rectangular prisms. The first is 2 in by $\frac{1}{2}$ in by $\frac{1}{2}$ in. The second is 1 in by $\frac{1}{2}$ in by $\frac{3}{2}$ in. What is the volume of the whole block in cubic inches?
questions.solution: The first prism has volume $2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$ cubic inch. The second has volume $1 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{3}{4}$ cubic inch. Together: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{5}{4}$ cubic inches.

questions.skill: Solve a volume problem in context
questions.stem: A tank has a base that is 2 feet by $\frac{3}{2}$ feet. It holds water $\frac{1}{2}$ foot deep. Then $\frac{3}{4}$ cubic foot more water is poured in. How deep is the water now?
questions.solution: The base area is $2 \times \frac{3}{2} = 3$ square feet. The extra water raises the level by $\frac{3}{4} \div 3 = \frac{1}{4}$ foot. The new depth is $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$ foot.

questions.skill: Fill a prism with unit cubes of fractional edge
questions.stem: A box is $\frac{3}{2}$ inches long, 1 inch wide and $\frac{3}{4}$ inch tall. It is packed with cubes whose edges are $\frac{1}{4}$ inch. How many cubes fill the box?
questions.solution: Along the length there are $\frac{3}{2} \div \frac{1}{4} = 6$ cubes, along the width 4 cubes and along the height 3 cubes. That is $6 \times 4 \times 3 = 72$ cubes.

questions.skill: Find a missing edge from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a base with an area of $\frac{3}{4}$ square meter and a volume of $\frac{9}{10}$ cubic meter. What is its height?
questions.solution: Height = volume $\div$ base area $= \frac{9}{10} \div \frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{10} \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{36}{30} = \frac{6}{5}$ meters.

questions.stem: A box is $\frac{7}{8}$ foot long, $\frac{9}{10}$ foot wide and $1\frac{1}{8}$ feet high. Which is the best estimate of its volume?
questions.solution: Round the edges: $\frac{7}{8}$ is about 1, $\frac{9}{10}$ is about 1 and $1\frac{1}{8}$ is about 1. The volume is about $1 \times 1 \times 1 = 1$ cubic foot. (The exact volume is $\frac{567}{640}$ cubic foot, close to 1.)

questions.skill: Solve a volume problem in context
questions.stem: Box A is $\frac{1}{2}$ foot by $\frac{1}{2}$ foot by 4 feet. Box B is $\frac{3}{4}$ foot by $\frac{1}{2}$ foot by 2 feet. Which statement is true?
choices: Box B holds $\frac{1}{4}$ cubic foot more than Box A
Box A holds $\frac{1}{2}$ cubic foot more than Box B
Box A and Box B hold the same amount
Box A holds $\frac{1}{4}$ cubic foot more than Box B
questions.answer: Box A holds $\frac{1}{4}$ cubic foot more than Box B
questions.solution: Box A: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times 4 = 1$ cubic foot. Box B: $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} \times 2 = \frac{3}{4}$ cubic foot. Box A holds $1 - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{1}{4}$ cubic foot more.

solve.answer: Box A holds $\frac{1}{4}$ cubic foot more than Box B

questions.skill: Fill a prism with unit cubes of fractional edge
questions.stem: A rectangular box is completely filled with 90 cubes. Each cube has edges of $\frac{1}{2}$ cm. What is the volume of the box in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Each cube has volume $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{8}$ cubic cm. The box has volume $90 \times \frac{1}{8} = \frac{90}{8} = \frac{45}{4}$, or $11\frac{1}{4}$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Identify a polygon from its vertices
questions.stem: The points $(2, 2)$, $(8, 2)$, $(8, 5)$ and $(2, 5)$ are joined in order, and the last point is joined back to the first. What shape is made?
choices: A rectangle that is not a square
questions.answer: A rectangle that is not a square
questions.solution: The sides are 6 units (bottom and top) and 3 units (left and right), and all four corners are square. That is a rectangle whose sides are not all equal.

solve.answer: A rectangle that is not a square
solve.work: Sides 6 (horizontal) and 3 (vertical), right angles: rectangle, not a square.

questions.stem: Which pair of points can be joined to make a horizontal segment?
questions.solution: A horizontal segment is flat, so both points have the same y-coordinate. Only $(2, 6)$ and $(9, 6)$ both have y-coordinate 6.

questions.skill: Length of a side that shares a coordinate
questions.stem: Points $A(2, 3)$ and $B(7, 3)$ are joined by a segment. How many units long is $\overline{AB}$?
questions.solution: Both points have y-coordinate 3, so the segment is horizontal. Its length is the difference of the x-coordinates: 7 - 2 = 5 units.

questions.skill: Length of a side that shares a coordinate
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices $(1, 6)$, $(1, 1)$ and $(5, 1)$. How many units long is the side from $(1, 1)$ to $(5, 1)$?
questions.solution: Both points have y-coordinate 1, so the side is horizontal. Its length is 5 - 1 = 4 units.

questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices $(0, 0)$, $(6, 0)$, $(6, 3)$ and $(0, 3)$. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: The bottom side runs from x = 0 to x = 6, so it is 6 units long. The left side runs from y = 0 to y = 3, so it is 3 units long. Perimeter = 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 units.

questions.skill: Length of a side that shares a coordinate
questions.stem: A square has vertices $(1, 2)$, $(9, 2)$, $(9, 10)$ and $(1, 10)$. How many units long is one side?
questions.solution: The bottom side runs from $(1, 2)$ to $(9, 2)$ at the same height, so its length is 9 - 1 = 8 units. All sides of a square are equal.

questions.stem: A vertical segment starts at $(5, 2)$ and goes up 4 units. What is the other endpoint?
questions.solution: A vertical segment keeps the same x-coordinate, 5. Going up 4 units makes the y-coordinate 2 + 4 = 6. The endpoint is $(5, 6)$.

questions.skill: Identify a polygon from its vertices
questions.stem: The points $A(1, 1)$, $B(4, 1)$, $C(4, 3)$, $D(2, 5)$ and $E(1, 3)$ are joined in order, and $E$ is joined back to $A$. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: There is one side from each point to the next: $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DE$ and $EA$. That makes 5 sides.

solve.work: Vertices A,B,C,D,E joined in a closed loop: 5 segments, a pentagon (non-self-intersecting).

questions.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are $(1, 1)$, $(6, 1)$ and $(6, 4)$. What is the fourth vertex?
questions.solution: The fourth vertex is above $(1, 1)$ and level with $(6, 4)$, so it has x-coordinate 1 and y-coordinate 4. The vertex is $(1, 4)$.

questions.skill: Length of a side that shares a coordinate
questions.stem: A segment joins $C(4, 1)$ and $D(4, 8)$. How many units long is it?
questions.solution: Both points have x-coordinate 4, so the segment is vertical. Its length is the difference of the y-coordinates: 8 - 1 = 7 units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle from the vertices
questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices $(2, 1)$, $(2, 9)$, $(7, 9)$ and $(7, 1)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The left side is 9 - 1 = 8 units long and the top side is 7 - 2 = 5 units long. Area = 8 x 5 = 40 square units.

questions.stem: A segment joins $(-2, -7)$ and $(-2, -1)$. How many units long is it?
questions.solution: Both points have x-coordinate -2, so the segment is vertical. The y-coordinates are on the same side of the x-axis, so subtract the distances: 7 - 1 = 6 units.

questions.skill: Length of a side that shares a coordinate
questions.stem: A right triangle has vertices $(1, 1)$, $(7, 1)$ and $(7, 5)$. Two of its sides are horizontal or vertical. What is the sum of the lengths of those two sides, in units?
questions.solution: The first side is horizontal: 7 - 1 = 6 units. The second side is vertical: 5 - 1 = 4 units. 6 + 4 = 10 units.

questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices $(-3, -2)$, $(4, -2)$, $(4, 3)$ and $(-3, 3)$. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: The bottom side runs from x = -3 to x = 4, so it is 3 + 4 = 7 units long. The right side runs from y = -2 to y = 3, so it is 2 + 3 = 5 units long. Perimeter = 2 x (7 + 5) = 24 units.

questions.stem: Points $A(-3, 4)$ and $B(5, 4)$ are joined by a segment. How many units long is $\overline{AB}$?
questions.solution: The points have the same y-coordinate, so the segment is horizontal. They are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so add the distances from the axis: 3 + 5 = 8 units.

questions.skill: Identify a polygon from its vertices
questions.stem: Which list of points, joined in order and closed, makes a rectangle?
questions.solution: A rectangle has a horizontal pair and a vertical pair of sides. Only the first list has the top side level with the bottom and both side edges straight up and down: the last point must be $(1, 3)$.

solve.work: (1,1),(5,1),(5,3),(1,3): sides 4 and 2, right angles. Others are not rectangles.

questions.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are $(-5, 2)$, $(1, 2)$ and $(1, -4)$. What is the fourth vertex?
questions.solution: The fourth vertex is directly below $(-5, 2)$ and level with $(1, -4)$. So its x-coordinate is -5 and its y-coordinate is -4.

questions.stem: A segment joins $(-4, 3)$ and $(-4, -6)$. How many units long is it?
questions.solution: The x-coordinates are equal, so the segment is vertical. The points are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so add 3 and 6: 3 + 6 = 9 units.

questions.skill: Identify a polygon from its vertices
questions.stem: The points $(-2, 1)$, $(3, 1)$, $(3, -4)$ and $(-2, -4)$ are joined in order and closed. Which statement is true?
choices: It is a square with sides of 6 units
It is a rectangle with sides of 3 and 5 units
It is a rectangle with sides of 4 and 5 units
It is a square with sides of 5 units
questions.answer: It is a square with sides of 5 units
questions.solution: The top side runs from x = -2 to x = 3, which is 2 + 3 = 5 units. The right side runs from y = 1 to y = -4, which is 1 + 4 = 5 units. All sides are 5 units with square corners, so it is a square.

solve.answer: It is a square with sides of 5 units
solve.work: Top side (-2,1)-(3,1): 5. Right side (3,1)-(3,-4): 5. All sides 5 with right angles: square, side 5.

questions.skill: Find an unknown coordinate from a length
questions.stem: A vertical segment joins $(3, 2)$ and $(3, k)$. It is 7 units long, and $k$ is greater than 2. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The segment is vertical, so its length is the difference of the y-coordinates. Since k is greater than 2, k - 2 = 7, so k = 9.

questions.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are $A(-3, 2)$, $B(5, 2)$ and $C(5, -4)$. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
questions.solution: AB is horizontal: 3 + 5 = 8 units. BC is vertical: 2 + 4 = 6 units. Perimeter = 2 x (8 + 6) = 28 units.

questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices $(-6, -3)$, $(-6, 5)$, $(3, 5)$ and $(3, -3)$. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: The left side runs from y = -3 to y = 5, so it is 3 + 5 = 8 units. The top side runs from x = -6 to x = 3, so it is 6 + 3 = 9 units. Perimeter = 2 x (8 + 9) = 34 units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle from the vertices
questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices $(-7, -2)$, $(5, -2)$, $(5, -9)$ and $(-7, -9)$. What is its area?
questions.solution: The top side is 7 + 5 = 12 units long. The right side is 9 - 2 = 7 units long. Area = 12 x 7 = 84 square units.

questions.skill: Find an unknown coordinate from a length
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 units. One side runs from $(-2, 3)$ to $(6, 3)$, and the other two vertices are above that side. What is the y-coordinate of those two vertices?
questions.solution: The given side is 2 + 6 = 8 units long. Half the perimeter is 15, so the height is 15 - 8 = 7 units. The other vertices are 7 units above y = 3, so their y-coordinate is 10.

solve.work: Side length 6 - (-2) = 8. 2(8 + w) = 30, w = 7. Vertices above: y = 3 + 7 = 10.

questions.skill: Length of a side that shares a coordinate
questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(-2, 1)$, $B(4, 1)$ and $C(4, 6)$. Which statement gives the lengths of $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{BC}$?
questions.solution: A and B share y-coordinate 1, and A is left of the y-axis, so AB = 2 + 4 = 6 units. B and C share x-coordinate 4, so BC = 6 - 1 = 5 units.

questions.stem: A square has one side from $(-1, 4)$ to $(-1, -5)$. What is the perimeter of the square in units?
questions.solution: The side is vertical and crosses the x-axis, so its length is 4 + 5 = 9 units. A square has four equal sides: 4 x 9 = 36 units.

questions.skill: Identify a polygon from its vertices
questions.stem: Which list of vertices, joined in order and closed, makes a square with sides of 4 units?
questions.solution: In the first list, the left side is 3 + 1 = 4 units, the top is 6 - 2 = 4 units, and the right side is 4 units, with square corners. The others have a side of 3 or 5 units, or a slanted side.

solve.work: Option 1 sides: 4,4,4,4 with right angles: square. Others: (6,0) not closing square; 5x4; 4x3.

questions.skill: Find an unknown coordinate from a length
questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices $(1, 2)$, $(1, 8)$, $(k, 8)$ and $(k, 2)$, with $k$ greater than 1. Its perimeter is 22 units. What is $k$?
questions.solution: The vertical sides are 8 - 2 = 6 units long. Half the perimeter is 11, so the horizontal side is 11 - 6 = 5 units long. Then k - 1 = 5, so k = 6.

solve.work: Height 8 - 2 = 6. Perimeter 2(w + 6) = 22 gives w = 5, so k - 1 = 5 and k = 6.

questions.stem: Mara says the segment from $(-8, 3)$ to $(5, 3)$ is 3 units long because 8 - 5 = 3. What is her mistake?
choices: The segment is vertical, so she should use the y-coordinates
The points are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so she should add 8 and 5
She should add 8 and 5 and then double the result
She should subtract 5 - 8 and write the result as -3
questions.answer: The points are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so she should add 8 and 5
questions.solution: Both y-coordinates are 3, so the segment is horizontal and the x-coordinates are used. -8 and 5 are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so the length is 8 + 5 = 13 units.

solve.answer: The points are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so she should add 8 and 5
solve.work: Horizontal segment from x=-8 to x=5: length 8 + 5 = 13, since the points are on opposite sides of the y-axis.

questions.stem: A polygon has vertices $(0, 0)$, $(6, 0)$, $(6, 2)$, $(3, 2)$, $(3, 5)$ and $(0, 5)$, joined in order and closed. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: Each side is horizontal or vertical. The lengths in order are 6, 2, 3, 3, 3 and 5 units. Their sum is 22 units.

questions.skill: Name a solid from the faces of its net
questions.stem: A net is made of 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. Which solid does it fold into?
questions.solution: A prism has two matching bases joined by rectangles. Two triangle bases and 3 rectangles make a triangular prism.

solve.work: 2 triangular ends + 3 rectangular sides = triangular prism.

questions.stem: How many faces does a square pyramid have, counting its base?
questions.solution: A square pyramid has 1 square base and 4 triangular faces, so $1 + 4 = 5$ faces.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The faces come in three matching pairs: $5 \times 3 = 15$, $5 \times 2 = 10$ and $3 \times 2 = 6$. Adding all six: $2 \times (15 + 10 + 6) = 62$.

questions.skill: Name a solid from the faces of its net
questions.stem: A net is made of 1 square and 4 triangles. Which solid does it fold into?
questions.solution: The square is the base and the 4 triangles are the sides that meet at the top point. This is a square pyramid.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: A cube has edges of 4 inches. What is its surface area, in square inches?
questions.solution: The cube has 6 square faces, each with area $4 \times 4 = 16$. The total is $6 \times 16 = 96$.

questions.stem: The net of a rectangular prism is made of 6 rectangles. Which statement is always true?
choices: All six rectangles are exactly the same size
Exactly four of the rectangles are the same size
The rectangles come in three pairs of matching sizes
No two of the rectangles are the same size
questions.answer: The rectangles come in three pairs of matching sizes
questions.solution: Opposite faces of a rectangular prism match, so the six rectangles always form three matching pairs. In a cube all six are the same size, and in a box with three different edges no more than two match, so the other statements are not always true.

solve.answer: The rectangles come in three pairs of matching sizes
solve.work: Opposite faces match: three pairs (true even for a cube).

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: One face of a cube has an area of 9 square centimeters. What is the cube's surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 matching faces: $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: The net of a triangular prism has 2 triangles, each with an area of 6 square cm, and 3 rectangles with areas of 12, 15 and 20 square cm. What is the surface area of the prism, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Add the areas of all 5 faces: $6 + 6 + 12 + 15 + 20 = 59$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a square pyramid from its triangular faces
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base 4 cm by 4 cm. Each of its 4 triangular faces has a base of 4 cm and a height of 5 cm. Which expression gives its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The base has area $4 \times 4 = 16$. Each triangle has area $\frac{4 \times 5}{2}$, and there are 4 of them. So the expression is $16 + 4 \times \frac{4 \times 5}{2}$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a pyramid from its net
questions.stem: The net of a square pyramid has one square with an area of 25 square centimeters and four identical triangles, each with an area of 20 square centimeters. What is the surface area of the pyramid, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The surface area is the area of all the faces in the net. The square is 25 and the four triangles are $4 \times 20 = 80$. The total is $25 + 80 = 105$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: A gift box is 10 cm long, 6 cm wide and 4 cm tall. How many square centimeters of paper are needed to cover the whole box with no overlap?
questions.solution: The paper must cover all 6 faces: $2 \times (10 \times 6 + 10 \times 4 + 6 \times 4) = 2 \times (60 + 40 + 24) = 248$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has right-triangle ends with sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm, and the prism is 10 cm long. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangle end has area $\frac{3 \times 4}{2} = 6$, so the two ends give 12. The three rectangles are $3 \times 10$, $4 \times 10$ and $5 \times 10$, which give $30 + 40 + 50 = 120$. The total is $12 + 120 = 132$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a square pyramid from its triangular faces
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base edge of 10 cm. Each of its 4 triangular faces has a height of 13 cm, measured along the face. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The base has area $10 \times 10 = 100$. Each triangle has area $\frac{10 \times 13}{2} = 65$, so 4 triangles give 260. The total is $100 + 260 = 360$.

questions.skill: Surface area of part of a solid
questions.stem: A box with no lid is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide and 3 inches tall. How many square inches of paint are needed to paint its outside, including the bottom but not the missing top?
questions.solution: A closed box has area $2 \times (8 \times 5 + 8 \times 3 + 5 \times 3) = 2 \times 79 = 158$. The missing top has area $8 \times 5 = 40$. So $158 - 40 = 118$.

questions.skill: Name a solid from the faces of its net
questions.stem: A net is made of 2 pentagons and 5 rectangles. Which solid does it fold into?
questions.solution: Two matching pentagon bases joined by 5 rectangles make a pentagonal prism. A prism has one rectangle for each side of its base.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: A cube has a surface area of 150 square inches. How long is one edge, in inches?
questions.solution: The 6 faces are the same, so one face has area $150 \div 6 = 25$ square inches. A square with area 25 has sides of 5 inches.

questions.skill: Surface area of a square pyramid from its triangular faces
questions.stem: Priya found the surface area of a square pyramid with a base edge of 6 cm and triangular faces of height 5 cm. She calculated $6 \times 6 + 4 \times 6 \times 5 = 156$. What did she forget to do?
choices: find half of base times height for each triangle
square the height of each triangle
add the area of a second square base
questions.answer: find half of base times height for each triangle
questions.solution: A triangle's area is half of its base times its height. Each triangle has area $\frac{6 \times 5}{2} = 15$, so the correct surface area is $36 + 4 \times 15 = 96$.

solve.answer: find half of base times height for each triangle
solve.work: Triangle area should be 6*5/2, she used 6*5.

questions.skill: Surface area of a square pyramid from its triangular faces
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base edge of 8 meters. Each of its 4 triangular faces has a height of 5 meters. What is the total area of the 4 triangular faces, in square meters?
questions.solution: Each triangle has area $\frac{8 \times 5}{2} = 20$. Four triangles give $4 \times 20 = 80$ square meters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular or triangular pyramid
questions.stem: A triangular pyramid has 4 faces that are all triangles with a base of 6 cm and a height of 5.2 cm. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangle has area $\frac{6 \times 5.2}{2} = 15.6$. Four triangles give $4 \times 15.6 = 62.4$.

questions.stem: How many faces does a hexagonal prism have in all?
questions.solution: A hexagonal prism has 2 hexagon bases and 6 rectangles, one for each side of the hexagon. That is $2 + 6 = 8$ faces.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has triangle ends with a base of 6 cm, a height of 4 cm, and two equal sides of 5 cm. The prism is 9 cm long. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each end has area $\frac{6 \times 4}{2} = 12$, so the two ends give 24. The three rectangles have a width of 9 and lengths 6, 5 and 5: $9 \times (6 + 5 + 5) = 144$. The total is $24 + 144 = 168$.

solve.work: Ends 2*(6*4/2) = 24; sides (6+5+5)*9 = 144; total 168. (3-4-5 check: sides 5 consistent.)

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism or cube
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 9 inches long and 5 inches wide, and its height is unknown. Its surface area is 202 square inches. What is its height, in inches?
questions.solution: The top and bottom give $2 \times 9 \times 5 = 90$. The four sides give $202 - 90 = 112$ square inches. Their total width around is $9 + 5 + 9 + 5 = 28$ inches, so the height is $112 \div 28 = 4$ inches.

questions.skill: Surface area of part of a solid
questions.stem: A cube with edges of 3 cm is glued on top of a cube with edges of 5 cm. The small cube's bottom face sits completely on the big cube's top face. What is the surface area of the whole solid, including its bottom, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The big cube alone has surface area $6 \times 25 = 150$. The small cube hides a 3 by 3 patch of the big cube's top, which takes away $9$. The small cube adds its own top ($9$) and its four sides ($4 \times 9 = 36$), but not its bottom, which is glued. The total is $150 - 9 + 9 + 36 = 186$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has right-triangle ends with legs of 6 cm and 8 cm and a longest side of 10 cm. The prism is 12 cm long and rests on its 8 cm by 12 cm rectangular face. What is the area of its surface that is not touching the table, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The two ends give $2 \times \frac{6 \times 8}{2} = 48$. The three rectangles give $(6 + 8 + 10) \times 12 = 288$. The total surface area is $48 + 288 = 336$. The face on the table has area $8 \times 12 = 96$, so the rest is $336 - 96 = 240$.

questions.stem: Every edge of a cube is doubled in length. How does the cube's surface area change?
questions.solution: Try an edge of 1: the surface area is $6 \times 1 = 6$. With an edge of 2 it is $6 \times 4 = 24$. Since $24 \div 6 = 4$, the surface area becomes 4 times as large.

questions.stem: Two cubes, each with edges of 2 cm, are glued face to face to make one long box. What is the surface area of the long box, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The long box is 4 cm by 2 cm by 2 cm, so its surface area is $2 \times (4 \times 2 + 4 \times 2 + 2 \times 2) = 2 \times 20 = 40$. Check: two separate cubes have $48$, and the glued faces hide $2 \times 4 = 8$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a square pyramid from its triangular faces
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base edge of 12 meters and a total surface area of 384 square meters. What is the height of each triangular face, in meters?
questions.solution: The base has area $12 \times 12 = 144$. The 4 triangles share $384 - 144 = 240$, so each has area $240 \div 4 = 60$. A triangle with base 12 and area 60 has height $\frac{2 \times 60}{12} = 10$.

questions.stem: Box A is a cube with edges of 4 units. Box B is a rectangular prism that is 2 units by 4 units by 8 units. Both have a volume of 64 cubic units. Which box has the smaller surface area, and by how much?
questions.solution: Box A: $6 \times 16 = 96$. Box B: $2 \times (2 \times 4 + 2 \times 8 + 4 \times 8) = 2 \times 56 = 112$. Box A is smaller by $112 - 96 = 16$.

questions.skill: Name a solid from the faces of its net
questions.stem: A pyramid has a rectangular base that is 4 cm by 6 cm, and its top point is above the base. Which list of faces makes up its net?
choices: one 4 by 6 rectangle and four triangles, two with base 4 and two with base 6
one 4 by 6 rectangle and four triangles, all with base 4
two 4 by 6 rectangles and four triangles, two with base 4 and two with base 6
one 4 by 6 rectangle and six triangles, three with base 4 and three with base 6
questions.answer: one 4 by 6 rectangle and four triangles, two with base 4 and two with base 6
questions.solution: Each triangle sits on one side of the base. A rectangle has 4 sides: two of length 4 and two of length 6, so the triangles have bases 4, 4, 6 and 6, and there is just one rectangle.

solve.answer: one 4 by 6 rectangle and four triangles, two with base 4 and two with base 6
solve.work: One rectangular base, four triangles on its four edges (two 4, two 6).

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular or triangular pyramid
questions.stem: The net of a triangular pyramid has a base that is a right triangle with sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Each of the three side triangles has a height of 6 cm, measured from the matching edge of the base. What is the surface area of the pyramid, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The base is a right triangle with legs 3 and 4: $\frac{3 \times 4}{2} = 6$. The side triangles have bases 3, 4 and 5 and height 6: $\frac{3 \times 6}{2} = 9$, $\frac{4 \times 6}{2} = 12$ and $\frac{5 \times 6}{2} = 15$, which add to 36. The total is $6 + 36 = 42$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Base right triangle legs 3,4: area 6. Faces: 3x6/2=9, 4x6/2=12, 5x6/2=15, sum 36. Total 6 + 36 = 42. (Consistent: apex above incenter, inradius 1.)

questions.stem: Room 12 is collecting data. Which question is a statistical question?
choices: How many books are on the top shelf of Room 12's bookcase right now?
How many pages are in the book that Ravi is reading right now?
How many books does each student in Room 12 read in a month?
How many students from Room 12 are at school today?
questions.answer: How many books does each student in Room 12 read in a month?
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. Students in Room 12 will read different numbers of books, so that question expects variability. Each of the others has just one answer.

solve.answer: How many books does each student in Room 12 read in a month?
solve.work: Only D gathers many varying values (each student, per month). A, B, C each have one answer.

questions.skill: Pick the question that is not statistical
questions.stem: The school office is planning lunch. Which of these questions is NOT statistical?
choices: How many minutes long is the lunch period at our school?
How many minutes does each student take to eat lunch at our school?
How many minutes do students spend on homework after lunch each night?
How many minutes does the bus ride take for each student at our school?
questions.answer: How many minutes long is the lunch period at our school?
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. The length of the lunch period is one fixed number, so no variability is expected. The other three will have different answers for different students.

solve.answer: How many minutes long is the lunch period at our school?
solve.work: The lunch period length is one fixed value; the others vary student to student.

questions.skill: Count the statistical questions in a list
questions.stem: How many of these four questions are statistical? (1) How tall is the flagpole at the park? (2) How tall are the trees in the park? (3) How many dogs are at the park right now? (4) How many dogs does each family on Oak Street own?
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. Questions (1) and (3) each have one answer. Questions (2) and (4) ask about many trees or families whose answers will differ. So 2 are statistical.

solve.work: (1) one value - no; (2) trees vary - yes; (3) one count - no; (4) varies by family - yes. Total 2.

questions.skill: Why a question is or is not statistical
questions.stem: Why is "How many hours do the students in our grade sleep on school nights?" a statistical question?
choices: Every student in the grade will give exactly the same answer
It asks about the hours of sleep of only one student
It can be answered without asking any student at all
Different students will probably give different answers
questions.answer: Different students will probably give different answers
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. Students do not all sleep the same number of hours, so the answers will vary.

solve.answer: Different students will probably give different answers
solve.work: Statistical because answers are expected to vary between students.

questions.stem: Mr. Diaz wants to learn about backpacks. Which question could he ask that is statistical?
choices: How much does Jada's backpack weigh when she gets to school today?
How much do sixth graders' backpacks weigh?
How many pockets are on the new backpack that Eli bought?
How much does the backpack on the nurse's desk weigh right now?
questions.answer: How much do sixth graders' backpacks weigh?
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. Many backpacks will have different weights. The others ask about one particular backpack.

solve.answer: How much do sixth graders' backpacks weigh?
solve.work: C asks about many backpacks with varying weights; the others are about one backpack.

questions.skill: Pick the question that is not statistical
questions.stem: How many of these four questions are NOT statistical? (1) On what date is the school picnic? (2) How many minutes long is a class period at our school? (3) How many minutes do the students in our grade spend reading each night? (4) Who is the principal of our school?
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. Questions (1), (2) and (4) each have one answer. Only question (3) expects different answers from different students. So 3 are not statistical.

solve.work: (1) fixed - not; (2) fixed - not; (3) varies - statistical; (4) one answer - not. 3 are NOT statistical.

questions.skill: Why a question is or is not statistical
questions.stem: Tom asks, "What is the height of the tallest mountain in North Carolina?" Why is this NOT a statistical question?
choices: It asks about a mountain, and mountains are not data
It has one answer, so no variability is expected
It asks for a number, and statistical questions ask for words
It cannot be answered by looking anything up
questions.answer: It has one answer, so no variability is expected
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. There is one tallest mountain with one height, so the answer does not vary.

solve.answer: It has one answer, so no variability is expected
solve.work: One mountain, one height: no variability expected.

questions.skill: Statistical questions with answers that are categories
questions.stem: Which of these is a statistical question about favorite lunches?
choices: What is the favorite lunch of our teacher, Mrs. Park?
What lunch is on the menu in the cafeteria today?
What is Sam's favorite lunch to bring from home?
What lunch does each sixth grader like the best?
questions.answer: What lunch does each sixth grader like the best?
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. Students in the grade will name different lunches, so the answers vary. The other questions ask about one person or one menu.

solve.answer: What lunch does each sixth grader like the best?
solve.work: A asks each sixth grader, so answers vary.

questions.stem: Ana asks every student in her class, "How many brothers and sisters do you have?" What should she expect about the answers?
choices: They will probably differ from student to student
Every student will give the same number of siblings
There will be only one possible answer to give
They cannot be numbers because they are about people
questions.answer: They will probably differ from student to student
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. Families are different, so Ana should expect different numbers. That variability is what makes the question statistical.

solve.answer: They will probably differ from student to student

questions.skill: Turn a question into a statistical question
questions.stem: Sam asks, "How tall is Sam?" Which question about height is a statistical question?
choices: How tall will Sam be when he is in high school?
How old is Sam on his next birthday?
How tall are the students in Sam's class?
How tall is Sam when he stands by the door today?
questions.answer: How tall are the students in Sam's class?
questions.solution: A statistical question is one where you expect the answers to vary, so you need to collect data from many people, things or times. The students in Sam's class have different heights. The other questions each have one answer.

solve.answer: How tall are the students in Sam's class?
solve.work: C asks heights of many students, which vary.

questions.stem: A shopper wants to compare prices. Which of these questions is statistical?
