questions.skill: Describe a data set with its center and spread
questions.stem: Which of these tells how spread out the values in a data set are?
questions.solution: The mean and the median describe the center of the data. The range, the highest value minus the lowest, describes how spread out the data are.

solve.work: Mean and median are measures of center; the range measures spread.

questions.stem: Ben scored 12, 16, 9 and 15 points in four games. What is the mean number of points he scored per game?
The ages of five cousins are 15, 11, 18, 12 and 14 years. What is the median age, in years?
questions.solution: Put the ages in order: 11, 12, 14, 15, 18. The middle age is 14.

questions.stem: Four students read 2, 4, 6 and 12 pages. What is the median number of pages?
questions.solution: The numbers are already in order. With four values, the median is the mean of the two middle ones: $\frac{4 + 6}{2} = 5$.

questions.stem: Four friends have 2, 4, 6 and 8 stickers. They put all their stickers together and share them equally. How many stickers does each friend get?
questions.solution: Together they have $2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20$ stickers. Shared equally among 4 friends, each gets $20 \div 4 = 5$. This is the mean.

solve.work: Total 2+4+6+8 = 20; 20/4 = 5 each (the mean as fair share).

questions.stem: The shortest plant in a garden is 12 cm tall and the tallest is 31 cm tall. What is the range of the plant heights, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least: $31 - 12 = 19$. Adding them gives 43, and 21.5 is the number halfway between them.

questions.skill: Describe a data set with its center and spread
questions.stem: Class A's test scores have a mean of 80 and a range of 5. Class B's test scores have a mean of 80 and a range of 30. Which statement is true?
choices: Class A's scores are more spread out than Class B's
Class B did better on average than Class A
Class A did better on average than Class B
Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
questions.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
questions.solution: The means are equal, so the classes did equally well on average. The range tells the spread, and Class B's range of 30 is larger than Class A's range of 5, so its scores are more spread out.

solve.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out than Class A's
solve.work: Equal means, so neither did better on average. Class B's range (30) is larger, so its scores are more spread out.

questions.stem: Mia's five quiz scores are 78, 85, 92, 88 and 87. What is the mean of her scores?
Six runners finished a race in 14, 12, 19, 15, 11 and 13 minutes. What is the median finishing time, in minutes?
questions.solution: Put the times in order: 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 19. With six values, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: $\frac{13 + 14}{2} = 13.5$.

questions.stem: Eight scores in order are 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 14, 16 and 18. The first quartile $Q_1$ is the median of the lower four values, and the third quartile $Q_3$ is the median of the upper four values. What is the interquartile range, $Q_3 - Q_1$?
questions.solution: The lower four values are 3, 5, 7, 9, so $Q_1 = \frac{5 + 7}{2} = 6$. The upper four values are 10, 14, 16, 18, so $Q_3 = \frac{14 + 16}{2} = 15$. The interquartile range is $15 - 6 = 9$.

questions.stem: The data set 6, 8, 12, 14 has a mean of 10. The mean absolute deviation is the mean of the distances of the values from the mean. What is the mean absolute deviation of this data set?
questions.solution: The distances from 10 are 4, 2, 2 and 4. Their mean is $\frac{4 + 2 + 2 + 4}{4} = 3$.

questions.skill: Describe a data set with its center and spread
questions.stem: Two bus routes were timed on five days. Route A took 10, 11, 10, 12 and 12 minutes. Route B took 5, 8, 12, 14 and 16 minutes. Both routes have a mean of 11 minutes. Which statement is correct?
choices: Route B is more predictable because its range is larger
Route A is more predictable because its range is smaller
Route A is more predictable because its mean is smaller
Both routes are equally predictable because the means are equal
questions.answer: Route A is more predictable because its range is smaller
questions.solution: Route A's range is $12 - 10 = 2$ minutes and Route B's range is $16 - 5 = 11$ minutes. The times for Route A vary less, so it is more predictable. The means are equal, so they do not separate the routes.

solve.answer: Route A is more predictable because its range is smaller
solve.work: Route A range 12 - 10 = 2; Route B range 16 - 5 = 11. Smaller spread means more predictable: Route A. Means are equal, so the mean-based option is false.

questions.skill: Choose between the mean and the median
questions.stem: Five students saved 10, 12, 11, 13 and 54 dollars. Which measure of center better describes a typical amount saved?
choices: The mean, because it is the best measure for every data set
The median, because it is always smaller than the mean
The median, because the very large value 54 pulls the mean up
The mean, because every value should count equally here
questions.answer: The median, because the very large value 54 pulls the mean up
questions.solution: The mean is $\frac{100}{5} = 20$ dollars, higher than four of the five amounts because of the 54. The median is 12 dollars, which is close to what most students saved.

solve.answer: The median, because the very large value 54 pulls the mean up
solve.work: Mean = 100/5 = 20, pulled up by the outlier 54; median 12 is typical. The median is not 'always smaller', so D is the correct reason.

questions.skill: Use the mean to find a missing value
questions.stem: The mean of four numbers is 7. Three of the numbers are 5, 8 and 9. What is the fourth number?
questions.solution: Four numbers with a mean of 7 add up to $4 \cdot 7 = 28$. The three known numbers add up to $5 + 8 + 9 = 22$, so the fourth is $28 - 22 = 6$.

questions.skill: Describe a data set with its center and spread
questions.stem: A data set is 20, 21, 19, 20 and 20. Which statement describes its median and range?
choices: The median is 20 and the range is 2
The median is 20 and the range is 1
The median is 19 and the range is 2
The median is 20 and the range is 21
questions.answer: The median is 20 and the range is 2
questions.solution: In order the values are 19, 20, 20, 20, 21. The middle value is 20, so the median is 20. The range is $21 - 19 = 2$.

solve.answer: The median is 20 and the range is 2

questions.stem: Four seedlings are 1.2, 0.8, 1.5 and 1.1 meters tall. What is the range of their heights, in meters?
questions.solution: The tallest is 1.5 meters and the shortest is 0.8 meters. The range is $1.5 - 0.8 = 0.7$ meters.

questions.stem: Which list of numbers has a median of 8?
questions.solution: In order, 12, 3, 8, 15, 6 becomes 3, 6, 8, 12, 15, with median 8. The list 3, 14, 8, 10, 12 has 8 in the middle only before it is ordered; its median is 10. The list 2, 2, 4, 12, 20 has a mean of 8, but its median is 4. The list 1, 4, 9, 10, 15 has a median of 9.

solve.work: A ordered 3,8,10,12,14 median 10. B median 9. C median 4. D ordered 3,6,8,12,15 median 8.

questions.skill: Choose between the mean and the median
questions.stem: The numbers 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18 have a mean of 14. A sixth number, 50, is added to the data. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: The new total is $10 + 12 + 14 + 16 + 18 + 50 = 120$. Divide by 6 numbers: $120 \div 6 = 20$. The one large value raised the mean from 14 to 20.

questions.skill: Choose between the mean and the median
questions.stem: The data 30, 32, 34, 36 and 38 have a mean of 34 and a median of 34. The value 4 is added to the data. Which statement is true?
choices: The mean decreases by 1 and the median decreases by 5
The mean and the median both decrease by 5
The mean decreases by 5 and the median stays the same
The mean decreases by 5 and the median decreases by 1
questions.answer: The mean decreases by 5 and the median decreases by 1
questions.solution: The new total is $170 + 4 = 174$ for 6 values, so the new mean is 29, which is 5 less. The new order is 4, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38, so the median is $\frac{32 + 34}{2} = 33$, which is only 1 less. The low value affects the mean much more than the median.

solve.answer: The mean decreases by 5 and the median decreases by 1

questions.stem: Ten scores in order are 55, 60, 62, 65, 70, 72, 75, 80, 90 and 95. The first quartile $Q_1$ is the median of the lower five values, and the third quartile $Q_3$ is the median of the upper five values. What is the interquartile range, $Q_3 - Q_1$?
questions.solution: The lower five values are 55, 60, 62, 65, 70, so $Q_1 = 62$. The upper five values are 72, 75, 80, 90, 95, so $Q_3 = 80$. The interquartile range is $80 - 62 = 18$.

questions.stem: A data set is 4, 6, 10, 12 and 18. The mean absolute deviation is the mean of the distances of the values from the mean. What is the mean absolute deviation of this data set?
questions.solution: The mean is $\frac{4 + 6 + 10 + 12 + 18}{5} = 10$. The distances from 10 are 6, 4, 0, 2 and 8. Their mean is $\frac{6 + 4 + 0 + 2 + 8}{5} = \frac{20}{5} = 4$.

questions.skill: Choose between the mean and the median
questions.stem: A data set is 4, 5, 5, 6, 7 and 40. Which pair of measures describes the typical value and the spread without being pulled by the 40? (Use the median of each half of the data for the quartiles.)
choices: The median, 5.5, and the interquartile range, 2
The mean, about 11.2, and the range, 36
The mean, about 11.2, and the interquartile range, 2
questions.answer: The median, 5.5, and the interquartile range, 2
questions.solution: The median is $\frac{5 + 6}{2} = 5.5$. The lower half is 4, 5, 5 and the upper half is 6, 7, 40, so $Q_1 = 5$, $Q_3 = 7$ and the interquartile range is 2. The mean and the range both use the 40, which is far from the other values.

solve.answer: The median, 5.5, and the interquartile range, 2
solve.work: Median (5+6)/2 = 5.5. Lower half 4,5,5: Q1 = 5; upper half 6,7,40: Q3 = 7; IQR = 2. Mean 67/6 = 11.17 and range 36 are both pulled by 40. So median 5.5 with IQR 2.

questions.skill: Use the mean to find a missing value
questions.stem: Maya wants a mean of 90 on her 5 tests. Her first four scores are 88, 92, 85 and 91. What score does she need on the fifth test?
questions.solution: Five tests with a mean of 90 need a total of $5 \cdot 90 = 450$. Her first four scores add to $88 + 92 + 85 + 91 = 356$. She needs $450 - 356 = 94$.

questions.skill: Describe a data set with its center and spread
questions.stem: The data set is 8, 9, 9, 10, 11, 11, 12. Which statement is correct?
choices: The mean is 10, the median is 9 and the range is 4
The mean is 10, the median is 10 and the range is 12
The mean is 10, the median is 10 and the range is 4
The mean is 9, the median is 10 and the range is 4
questions.answer: The mean is 10, the median is 10 and the range is 4
questions.solution: The total is 70, and $70 \div 7 = 10$, so the mean is 10. The middle (4th) value is 10, so the median is 10. The range is $12 - 8 = 4$.

solve.answer: The mean is 10, the median is 10 and the range is 4

questions.stem: Ten students were asked how many pets they have. One student has 0 pets, four have 1 pet, three have 2 pets and two have 3 pets. What is the mean number of pets?
questions.solution: The total number of pets is $0 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 4 + 2 \cdot 3 + 3 \cdot 2 = 16$. Divide by 10 students: $16 \div 10 = 1.6$. Averaging 0, 1, 2 and 3 would ignore how many students have each number and gives 1.5.

questions.skill: Describe a data set with its center and spread
questions.stem: A teacher adds 5 points to every student's test score. What happens to the mean and the range of the scores?
choices: The mean and the range both increase by 5
The mean increases by 5 and the range stays the same
The mean stays the same and the range increases by 5
The mean increases by 5 and the range decreases by 5
questions.answer: The mean increases by 5 and the range stays the same
questions.solution: Every score moves up by 5, so the mean moves up by 5. The highest and lowest scores both go up by 5, so their difference, the range, does not change.

solve.answer: The mean increases by 5 and the range stays the same
solve.work: Adding 5 to every value shifts the mean up 5; max and min both rise 5 so the range is unchanged.

questions.skill: Use the mean to find a missing value
questions.stem: Four numbers are 5, 9, 12 and $x$, and their mean is 10. What is the median of the four numbers?
questions.solution: The total must be $4 \cdot 10 = 40$, so $x = 40 - 26 = 14$. In order the numbers are 5, 9, 12, 14. The median is the mean of the middle two: $\frac{9 + 12}{2} = 10.5$.

questions.stem: A dot plot shows how many pets each of 10 students has. Written out: 0 pets: 2 dots, 1 pet: 4 dots, 2 pets: 3 dots, 3 pets: 1 dot. How many students have exactly 2 pets?
questions.solution: Each dot is one student. The column for 2 pets has 3 dots, so 3 students have exactly 2 pets.

questions.stem: A box plot is drawn from five numbers. Which list names them?
choices: Minimum, lower quartile, mean, upper quartile, maximum
Range, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, interquartile range
Minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum
questions.answer: Minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum
questions.solution: A box plot marks the least value, the lower quartile, the median, the upper quartile and the greatest value.

solve.answer: Minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum
solve.work: Five-number summary: minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum.

questions.stem: A histogram of quiz scores has these bars: 60-69: 3 students, 70-79: 8 students, 80-89: 6 students, 90-99: 2 students. How many students are shown in all?
questions.solution: Each bar shows how many students fall in that interval. Add the bars: $3 + 8 + 6 + 2 = 19$.

questions.stem: A box plot shows how many minutes students spent on homework. Its smallest value is 12 and its largest value is 40. What is the range, in minutes?
questions.solution: The range is the largest value minus the smallest: $40 - 12 = 28$ minutes.

questions.stem: In a box plot, what does the line drawn inside the box show?
choices: The largest value in the data
questions.solution: The line inside the box marks the median, the middle value of the data.

solve.work: The line inside the box is the median.

questions.skill: Building a display from a data set
questions.stem: The data 3, 5, 5, 6, 3, 5, 7 are shown on a dot plot. How many dots are above the number 5?
questions.solution: Count how many times 5 appears in the data: it appears 3 times, so there are 3 dots above 5.

solve.work: Values equal to 5: three of them, so 3 dots above 5.

questions.stem: Which statement describes a histogram?
choices: It shows how many values fall in each interval.
It shows every data value as its own dot.
It shows only the least, middle and greatest values.
It shows the data split into four equal parts.
questions.answer: It shows how many values fall in each interval.
questions.solution: A histogram groups the data into equal-width intervals and uses the height of each bar to show how many values are in that interval.

solve.answer: It shows how many values fall in each interval.
solve.work: A histogram shows counts per interval.

questions.stem: A dot plot of shoe sizes shows: size 5: 2 dots, size 6: 4 dots, size 7: 6 dots, size 8: 3 dots. Which shoe size is the most common?
questions.solution: The most common size is the one with the most dots. Size 7 has 6 dots, more than any other size.

questions.stem: A histogram shows the ages of 20 people. The tallest bar is for ages 10 to 14. Which statement must be true?
choices: Everyone in the group is between 10 and 14 years old.
The oldest person in the group is 14 years old.
More people are in 10 to 14 than in any other interval.
Exactly 10 people in the group are in the 10 to 14 interval.
questions.answer: More people are in 10 to 14 than in any other interval.
questions.solution: The height of a bar is the number of values in that interval. The tallest bar belongs to the interval with the most people. The other statements need not be true.

solve.answer: More people are in 10 to 14 than in any other interval.
solve.work: The tallest bar means that interval has the greatest count.

questions.stem: A box plot of quiz scores has whiskers ending at 4 and 10. Its box runs from 6 to 9, with a line inside the box at 8. What is the upper quartile?
questions.solution: The right-hand end of the box is the upper quartile. The box runs from 6 to 9, so the upper quartile is 9.

solve.work: The box runs Q1 = 6 to Q3 = 9. Upper quartile 9.

questions.stem: A box plot shows a minimum of 20, a lower quartile of 35, a median of 48, an upper quartile of 60 and a maximum of 82. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The interquartile range is the length of the box: upper quartile minus lower quartile. $60 - 35 = 25$.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to show how many students scored in each of the groups 60-69, 70-79, 80-89 and 90-99. Which display is made for this?
choices: A number line with the mean marked
questions.solution: A histogram groups values into equal intervals and shows a count for each. A dot plot shows each separate value, and a box plot shows five summary numbers.

questions.stem: A dot plot shows the number of books 12 students read last week: 1 book: 2 dots, 2 books: 5 dots, 3 books: 4 dots, 4 books: 1 dot. How many students read more than 2 books?
questions.solution: More than 2 books means 3 or 4 books. That is $4 + 1 = 5$ students.

questions.stem: Two box plots show test scores. Class A: minimum 40, lower quartile 55, median 70, upper quartile 85, maximum 100. Class B: minimum 50, lower quartile 60, median 70, upper quartile 80, maximum 90. Which statement is true?
choices: Class B has the higher median score of the two classes.
Class A's middle half is more spread out than Class B's.
Class B has the larger range of scores of the two classes.
Class A has the lower maximum score of the two classes.
questions.answer: Class A's middle half is more spread out than Class B's.
questions.solution: The medians are equal. The interquartile range is $85 - 55 = 30$ for Class A and $80 - 60 = 20$ for Class B, so the middle half of Class A is more spread out. Class A also has the larger range and the higher maximum.

solve.answer: Class A's middle half is more spread out than Class B's.
solve.work: IQR A = 30, B = 20, so A middle half more spread. A max 100 > 90; B range 40 < 60; medians equal 70.

questions.stem: A histogram of student heights in centimeters has these bars: 140-149: 4, 150-159: 9, 160-169: 7, 170-179: 2. How many students are shorter than 160 cm?
questions.solution: Students shorter than 160 cm are in the first two bars: $4 + 9 = 13$.

questions.stem: A set of 15 test scores is shown four ways. Which display lets you read each exact score?
choices: The dot plot of the scores
The box plot of the scores
questions.answer: The dot plot of the scores
questions.solution: A dot plot puts a dot at each value, so every exact score can be read. A histogram only counts scores within each interval, and a box plot shows only five summary numbers.

solve.answer: The dot plot of the scores
solve.work: A dot plot shows each value; histograms and box plots summarise.

questions.skill: Building a display from a data set
questions.stem: These 10 ages are grouped into a histogram: 11, 12, 12, 13, 14, 16, 16, 17, 18, 19. The intervals are 10-12, 13-15, 16-18 and 19-21. How tall is the bar for 16-18?
questions.solution: The ages in 16-18 are 16, 16, 17 and 18. That is 4 values, so the bar has height 4.

questions.stem: In a box plot, about what part of the data lies inside the box?
questions.solution: The box runs from the lower quartile to the upper quartile. One quarter of the data lies below the box, one quarter above it, and the other half is inside.

solve.work: Box spans Q1 to Q3: about 50%.

questions.stem: A dot plot of leaf lengths in centimeters shows: 4 cm: 1 dot, 5 cm: 3 dots, 6 cm: 4 dots, 7 cm: 2 dots, 9 cm: 2 dots. What is the range, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least. The least length is 4 cm and the greatest is 9 cm, so the range is $9 - 4 = 5$ cm.

questions.skill: Building a display from a data set
questions.stem: The data set 5, 7, 8, 8, 9, 10, 12, 15 will be shown in a box plot. What is the upper quartile?
questions.solution: There are 8 values, so the upper half is the last four: 9, 10, 12, 15. Its median is the mean of the middle two, $\frac{10 + 12}{2} = 11$.

questions.stem: A class's test scores are shown in a histogram and in a box plot. Which question can the histogram answer that the box plot cannot?
choices: What was the median score of the class?
What was the highest score in the class?
What was the interquartile range of the scores?
How many students scored from 80 to 89?
questions.answer: How many students scored from 80 to 89?
questions.solution: A histogram shows how many values are in each interval. A box plot gives the median, the highest score and the interquartile range, but not a count for an interval.

solve.answer: How many students scored from 80 to 89?
solve.issues: Assumes the histogram uses an 80-89 interval, which is not stated; minor.
solve.work: A box plot gives median, IQR, max but not counts in an interval; a histogram with an 80-89 bar does.

questions.stem: Which of these can you NOT find from a box plot?
choices: How many values are in the data set
The interquartile range of the data
questions.answer: How many values are in the data set
questions.solution: A box plot shows the minimum, quartiles, median and maximum, so the median, range and interquartile range can be found. It does not show how many values there are.

solve.answer: How many values are in the data set
solve.work: A box plot does not show the number of values.

questions.stem: Box plot A has a minimum of 10, lower quartile 20, median 30, upper quartile 40 and maximum 70. Box plot B has a minimum of 20, lower quartile 25, median 30, upper quartile 35 and maximum 50. How much larger is the interquartile range of A than that of B?
questions.solution: The interquartile range of A is $40 - 20 = 20$ and that of B is $35 - 25 = 10$. The difference is $20 - 10 = 10$.

questions.stem: A histogram of 22 values has these bars: 0-9: 8, 10-19: 2, 20-29: 5, 30-39: 4, 40-49: 3. In which interval does the median lie?
questions.solution: With 22 values the median is the mean of the 11th and 12th values. The first two bars hold $8 + 2 = 10$ values, and the third bar holds the 11th through 15th. So the median is in 20 to 29, not in the tallest bar.

solve.work: Median between 11th and 12th values. Cumulative: 8, 10, 15. Both in 20-29.

questions.stem: A dot plot of 9 values shows: 1: 1 dot, 2: 3 dots, 3: 2 dots, 4: 2 dots, 5: 1 dot. What is the median?
questions.solution: In order the values are 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5. The middle (5th) value is 3.

questions.stem: A box plot of race times in minutes has a minimum of 12, lower quartile 14, median 15, upper quartile 20 and maximum 30. Which statement is true?
choices: Half of the times are between 12 and 14 minutes.
More than half of the times are above 20 minutes.
Times above the median are more spread out than below.
The median is closer to the maximum than to the minimum.
questions.answer: Times above the median are more spread out than below.
questions.solution: From the median to the maximum is $30 - 15 = 15$ minutes, while from the minimum to the median is only $15 - 12 = 3$ minutes. A quarter of the times are between 12 and 14, a quarter are above 20, and the median is closer to the minimum.

solve.answer: Times above the median are more spread out than below.
solve.work: Above median: 15 to 30 (span 15); below: 12 to 15 (span 3). More spread above. Only 25% above 20; median 3 from min, 15 from max; 25% between 12 and 14.

questions.skill: Building a display from a data set
questions.stem: Twelve students' practice times in minutes are 12, 25, 18, 30, 22, 15, 28, 35, 20, 24, 31, 19. They are grouped into a histogram with intervals 10-19, 20-29 and 30-39. How many more values are in the tallest bar than in the shortest bar?
questions.solution: The counts are 4 in 10-19 (12, 18, 15, 19), 5 in 20-29 (25, 22, 28, 20, 24) and 3 in 30-39 (30, 35, 31). The tallest bar has 5 and the shortest has 3, a difference of 2.

questions.stem: A set of 12 values is shown in a histogram with intervals 0-9, 10-19 and 20-29. What can you NOT find from the histogram?
choices: How many values are in each interval
Which interval has the most values
Which interval holds the largest value
The exact value of each data point
questions.answer: The exact value of each data point
questions.solution: A histogram shows how many values fall in each interval, so the counts, the tallest bar and the interval holding the largest value can all be found. The exact values inside an interval are not shown.

solve.answer: The exact value of each data point
solve.work: A histogram groups values; exact values are lost.

questions.stem: A histogram of 40 values has these bars: 0-9: 5, 10-19: 9, 20-29: 12, 30-39: 8, 40-49: 6. What fraction of the values are 20 or more?
questions.solution: The values 20 or more are in the last three bars: $12 + 8 + 6 = 26$. The fraction is $\frac{26}{40} = \frac{13}{20}$.

questions.stem: A teacher recorded the number of books each of 9 students read in a month: 3, 5, 4, 6, 5, 2, 7, 5, 4. How many observations are in this data set?
questions.solution: Each student gives one value, so each value is one observation. Count the values: 3, 5, 4, 6, 5, 2, 7, 5, 4 is 9 values. Repeated values still count, so there are 9 observations.

questions.skill: Identify the attribute and its unit
questions.stem: Ana measured how tall each of 12 sunflowers is, in centimeters. What is the attribute being measured, and what is its unit?
choices: The number of sunflowers, in centimeters
Height of a sunflower, in sunflowers
Height of a sunflower, in centimeters
questions.answer: Height of a sunflower, in centimeters
questions.solution: Ana measured how tall each sunflower is, so the attribute is the height of a sunflower. Height is measured in centimeters. The 12 is how many observations there are, not what is measured.

solve.answer: Height of a sunflower, in centimeters
solve.work: The attribute is the height of each sunflower; the unit is centimeters.

questions.stem: Four friends scored 6, 8, 9 and 5 points in a game. What is the mean score?
questions.solution: Add the scores: 6 + 8 + 9 + 5 = 28. Divide by the number of scores: 28 / 4 = 7.

questions.stem: The ages of five cousins are 7, 12, 9, 15 and 10. What is the median age?
questions.solution: Put the ages in order: 7, 9, 10, 12, 15. The median is the middle value, which is 10.

questions.stem: The daily high temperatures, in degrees Fahrenheit, for one week were 71, 68, 75, 80, 73, 66 and 77. What is the range of the temperatures?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value. The greatest is 80 and the least is 66, so the range is 80 - 66 = 14 degrees.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a data set
questions.stem: The numbers of pets in 10 households are 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6. Which best describes the shape of the data?
choices: Skewed right, with the peak at 4
Skewed left, with the peak at 4
questions.solution: The values pile up at 4 and fall away evenly on both sides: two values at 3 and two at 5, one at 2 and one at 6. The data are symmetric with the peak at 4.

solve.work: Frequencies: 2:1, 3:2, 4:4, 5:2, 6:1. Mirror image about 4, peak at 4.

questions.stem: Which measure of variability is found by subtracting the least value from the greatest value?
questions.solution: Subtracting the least value from the greatest value gives the range. The mean and the median describe the center, and the mean absolute deviation is found from distances to the mean.

solve.work: Greatest minus least is the range.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a data set
questions.stem: In the data set 12, 14, 13, 15, 14, 52, 13, which value is far from all the others (an outlier)?
questions.solution: Most values are between 12 and 15. The value 52 is far above the rest, so it is the outlier.

solve.work: Values cluster 12-15; 52 is far from the rest.

questions.stem: Three plates hold 4, 7 and 10 cookies. The cookies are moved so that each plate holds the same number. How many cookies are on each plate?
questions.solution: There are 4 + 7 + 10 = 21 cookies. Shared equally among 3 plates, each plate has 21 / 3 = 7 cookies. This is the mean of 4, 7 and 10.

solve.work: Total 4+7+10=21; shared equally among 3 plates: 21/3=7 (the mean as a fair share).

questions.stem: A data set lists the number of goals scored in each of 15 soccer games. What does the number 15 tell you?
choices: The total number of goals scored
The most goals scored in one game
The mean number of goals per game
questions.solution: Each game gives one value, so the 15 values are 15 observations and the 15 tells how many games there were. It is not a total, a greatest value or a mean.

solve.work: 15 is the number of observations, i.e. games played.

questions.stem: Eight students had these quiz scores: 14, 9, 17, 12, 20, 15, 11, 18. What is the median score?
questions.solution: Put the scores in order: 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 20. With 8 values the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th values, 14 and 15. (14 + 15) / 2 = 14.5.

questions.stem: A class of 20 students was asked how many siblings they have. 4 students have 0 siblings, 9 have 1 sibling, 5 have 2 siblings and 2 have 3 siblings. What is the mean number of siblings?
questions.solution: Find the total number of siblings: 0 x 4 + 1 x 9 + 2 x 5 + 3 x 2 = 0 + 9 + 10 + 6 = 25. Divide by the 20 students: 25 / 20 = 1.25.

questions.stem: Ten runners finished a race in these times, in minutes: 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 18, 20. What is the interquartile range (IQR) of the times?
questions.solution: The 10 values are already in order. The lower half is 4, 6, 7, 9, 10 and its median is Q1 = 7. The upper half is 12, 13, 15, 18, 20 and its median is Q3 = 15. IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 15 - 7 = 8.

questions.stem: The heights of four plants are 10, 14, 15 and 21 centimeters. The mean height is 15 centimeters. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the heights?
questions.solution: Find how far each height is from the mean of 15: 5, 1, 0 and 6. Add these distances: 5 + 1 + 0 + 6 = 12. Divide by 4 plants: 12 / 4 = 3 centimeters.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a data set
questions.stem: The numbers of texts sent in one day by 10 students are 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 9, 18, 31. Which best describes the shape of the data?
choices: Skewed left, with a few extremely small values
Skewed right, with a few very large values
Two clusters, with a gap in the middle
questions.answer: Skewed right, with a few very large values
questions.solution: Most students sent between 3 and 9 texts, and a few sent many more (18 and 31). The values stretch out to the right, so the data are skewed right.

solve.answer: Skewed right, with a few very large values
solve.work: Most values 3-9 with a long tail to 18 and 31: skewed right.

questions.skill: Identify the attribute and its unit
questions.stem: Each of 18 families reported its monthly electric bill, in dollars. Which statement correctly describes this data set?
choices: There are 18 observations, and each is a family measured in dollars
There is 1 observation, which is the total of the bills, measured in families
There are 18 observations, and each is a bill measured in families
There are 18 observations, and each is a bill measured in dollars
questions.answer: There are 18 observations, and each is a bill measured in dollars
questions.solution: Each family gives one bill, so there are 18 observations. Each observation is an amount of money, so its unit is dollars.

solve.answer: There are 18 observations, and each is a bill measured in dollars
solve.work: 18 families, each observation is one bill in dollars.

questions.skill: Choose the best measure of center or variability
questions.stem: The prices of 7 homes in a small town, in thousands of dollars, are 150, 160, 165, 170, 175, 180 and 900. Which measure is better for describing the center of these prices?
choices: The median, because a very large price pulls the mean up
The mean, because it uses every one of the values
The median, because the median is always greater than the mean
The mean, because the data are symmetric
questions.answer: The median, because a very large price pulls the mean up
questions.solution: The price 900 is far above the others and pulls the mean up to about 271. The median, 170, is not pulled by an extreme value, so it describes a typical home better.

solve.answer: The median, because a very large price pulls the mean up
solve.work: 900 is an extreme value that pulls the mean up; median resists it.

questions.stem: The mean of the data set 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 is 10. The value 40 is added to the data set. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: The new data set has 6 values with a total of 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14 + 40 = 90. The new mean is 90 / 6 = 15. The single large value raised the mean from 10 to 15.

questions.stem: Class A scored from 60 to 100 on a test, and class B scored from 75 to 95. How much greater is the range of class A's scores than the range of class B's scores?
questions.solution: Class A's range is 100 - 60 = 40. Class B's range is 95 - 75 = 20. The difference is 40 - 20 = 20.

questions.stem: Which data set has a median of 8?
questions.solution: The median of five ordered values is the 3rd value. In 3, 5, 8, 9, 20 the 3rd value is 8. The other sets have medians 9, 6 and 11 (the set 2, 4, 6, 12, 16 has a mean of 8, but its median is 6).

solve.work: Medians: A 9, B 8, C 6, D 11. Only B has median 8.

questions.stem: The mean of five test scores is 82. Four of the scores are 78, 85, 90 and 76. What is the fifth score?
questions.solution: Five scores with a mean of 82 have a total of 5 x 82 = 410. The four known scores add to 78 + 85 + 90 + 76 = 329. The fifth score is 410 - 329 = 81.

questions.stem: Six swimmers had these times, in seconds: 12.4, 11.8, 13.1, 12.0, 11.6, 12.9. What is the median time, in seconds?
questions.solution: Put the times in order: 11.6, 11.8, 12.0, 12.4, 12.9, 13.1. With 6 values the median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th values: (12.0 + 12.4) / 2 = 12.2 seconds.

questions.stem: Six backpacks weigh 15, 21, 24, 26, 29 and 35 pounds. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the weights, in pounds?
questions.solution: The total is 15 + 21 + 24 + 26 + 29 + 35 = 150, so the mean is 150 / 6 = 25. The distances from 25 are 10, 4, 1, 1, 4 and 10, which add to 30. MAD = 30 / 6 = 5 pounds.

questions.stem: Set P is 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and set Q is 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Both sets have a mean of 8. Which statement is true?
choices: Set Q has the greater MAD, 2.4 compared with 1.2
The two sets have the same MAD, because the means are equal
Set P has the greater MAD, 12 compared with 6
Set P has the greater MAD, 2.4 compared with 1.2
questions.answer: Set P has the greater MAD, 2.4 compared with 1.2
questions.solution: Set P: the distances from 8 are 4, 2, 0, 2, 4, which add to 12, so MAD = 12 / 5 = 2.4. Set Q: the distances are 2, 1, 0, 1, 2, which add to 6, so MAD = 6 / 5 = 1.2. Set P is more spread out. (The totals 12 and 6 must still be divided by 5.)

solve.answer: Set P has the greater MAD, 2.4 compared with 1.2
solve.work: P deviations 4,2,0,2,4: sum 12, MAD 2.4. Q deviations 2,1,0,1,2: sum 6, MAD 1.2. P greater.

questions.skill: Describe the shape of a data set
questions.stem: The ages of ten people at a party are 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 41, 42, 43 and 45. Which statement best describes the pattern in the data?
choices: One cluster from 5 to 45, with the age 45 as an outlier above the rest
Two clusters, from 5 to 9 and from 41 to 45, with a gap
Symmetric about the middle, with the peak at 7
Skewed right, with a single outlier at the age 5
questions.answer: Two clusters, from 5 to 9 and from 41 to 45, with a gap
questions.solution: Six ages are between 5 and 9 and four are between 41 and 45, with nothing between 9 and 41. That is two clusters with a gap. No single value stands alone as an outlier, and the data are not symmetric.

solve.answer: Two clusters, from 5 to 9 and from 41 to 45, with a gap
solve.work: Values 5-9 and 41-45 with nothing between: two clusters with a gap.

questions.skill: Choose the best measure of center or variability
questions.stem: At a company, most employees earn between 40 and 60 thousand dollars a year, but the owners earn more than 500 thousand dollars. Which pair of measures best summarizes the center and variability of the salaries?
questions.solution: The data are skewed with large outliers. The mean, the range and the MAD are all pulled by the outliers. The median and the IQR are not, so they best describe the typical salary and the spread of the middle half.

solve.work: Extreme high salaries skew the data; median and IQR are resistant.

questions.stem: The IQR of the number of minutes 30 students spent reading last night is 12. Which statement is correct?
choices: The middle half of the times is spread over 12 minutes
All 30 of the students' times are spread over 12 minutes
On average, the students read for exactly 12 minutes
Half of the students read for exactly 12 minutes
questions.answer: The middle half of the times is spread over 12 minutes
questions.solution: The IQR is Q3 - Q1, the width of the interval holding the middle half of the values. So the middle half of the times are spread over 12 minutes. It is not the range, a mean or a typical time.

solve.answer: The middle half of the times is spread over 12 minutes
solve.work: IQR = Q3-Q1, the spread of the middle 50% of data.

questions.stem: The data set 3, 5, 6, 8, 10 has a median of 6. The value 100 is added to the data set. What is the new median?
questions.solution: The new data set 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 100 has 6 values, so the median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th values: (6 + 8) / 2 = 7. The large value moved the median only from 6 to 7.

solve.work: New set 3,5,6,8,10,100 (6 values); middle two 6 and 8; median 7.

questions.skill: Identify the attribute and its unit
questions.stem: The mean heart rate of 15 athletes after a race was 142 beats per minute. Which sentence reports the mean correctly?
choices: The mean heart rate of the 15 athletes was 142 beats per minute
The mean heart rate of the 15 athletes was 142 athletes per minute
The mean number of athletes was 142 beats per minute
The mean heart rate of the 15 athletes was 142 beats in total
questions.answer: The mean heart rate of the 15 athletes was 142 beats per minute
questions.solution: The attribute is heart rate, and its unit is beats per minute. A correct sentence gives the attribute, the number and the unit, and does not turn the 15 athletes into a unit.

solve.answer: The mean heart rate of the 15 athletes was 142 beats per minute
solve.work: Mean keeps the unit of the data: beats per minute.
